A repeat-expansion disorder can therefore yield a false-negative exome.

whyWrongByChoice.A: NGS detection of small indels is good.
whyWrongByChoice.C: NGS detection of SNVs is excellent, so this is not a limitation of the technique.
whyWrongByChoice.D: SNP-arrays are targeted genotyping panels for SNPs, CNVs, and LOH; they are not described as the method for repeat expansions.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Higher depth improves detection (for example, of low-level mosaicism); excessive depth does not cause a negative result.

questions.topicName: Molecular Biology Techniques (2 of 3), DNA analysis

questions.stem: A biotechnology company running a CRISPR-based clinical trial for sickle cell disease must confirm that edited hematopoietic cells have increased fetal (gamma-globin) hemoglobin mRNA. The team wants precise, sensitive quantification of this single, known transcript. Which method is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bulk RNA sequencing (RNA-seq)

choices.label: B
choices.text: RT-qPCR (real-time PCR)

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sanger sequencing of cDNA

choices.label: D
choices.text: Southern blot of genomic DNA

choices.label: E
choices.text: Western blot for hemoglobin

explanation.summary: RT-qPCR is the tool for precise, targeted quantification of a known transcript such as fetal-globin mRNA.
explanation.whyCorrect: RT-qPCR first reverse-transcribes RNA to cDNA and then measures fluorescence at each amplification cycle, giving very high sensitivity and precision for a specific, known gene. This makes it ideal for assessing editing efficiency by quantifying fetal-globin expression in edited cells.

whyWrongByChoice.A: RNA-seq is a global, exploratory method with only moderate sensitivity and lower precision, so it is not the best choice for precise quantification of one known low-abundance transcript.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Sanger sequencing determines a nucleotide sequence but does not quantify gene expression.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Southern blot detects specific DNA sequences, not RNA expression levels.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Western blot detects protein, not the mRNA transcript being quantified here.

questions.topicName: Molecular Biology Techniques (3 of 3), RNA analysis

questions.stem: In the same trial, the FDA requires the team to screen for any unintended, genome-wide changes in gene expression between CRISPR-edited and non-edited cells, without specifying a predefined list of genes. Which technique best meets this requirement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Absolute qPCR using a standard curve

choices.label: B
choices.text: Northern blot

choices.label: C
choices.text: RNA sequencing

choices.label: D
choices.text: RT-qPCR

choices.label: E
choices.text: Western blot

explanation.summary: RNA-seq gives a transcriptome-wide, exploratory readout able to flag unexpected dysregulated genes.
explanation.whyCorrect: RNA-seq uses next-generation sequencing to analyze the entire transcriptome, so it can identify thousands of up- or downregulated genes between edited and non-edited cells without requiring a predefined target list, which is exactly what off-target screening needs.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Absolute qPCR quantifies a single known target against a standard curve and is likewise targeted, not genome-wide.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Northern blot analyzes one or a few known RNA species, not the whole transcriptome.
whyWrongByChoice.D: RT-qPCR is a targeted method requiring specific primers for known genes, so it cannot survey unanticipated changes across the whole transcriptome.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Western blot measures protein levels, not genome-wide transcript changes.

questions.topicName: Molecular Biology Techniques (3 of 3), RNA analysis

questions.stem: A researcher measures gene X by RT-qPCR in tumor tissue (condition A, Ct = 19) and in matched normal tissue (condition B, Ct = 25). Which conclusion is best supported by these Ct values?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Gene X is expressed equally in both tissues

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gene X is more highly expressed in the normal tissue

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gene X is more highly expressed in the tumor tissue

choices.label: D
choices.text: The tumor sample had a lower initial concentration of target

choices.label: E
choices.text: The tumor sample required more cycles to cross the threshold

explanation.summary: A lower Ct reflects a higher starting amount of target, so lower Ct means higher expression.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ct is inversely proportional to the initial amount of target. The tumor has the lower Ct (19 < 25), meaning fewer cycles were needed to exceed background, indicating a higher initial target concentration and therefore higher expression of gene X.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The Ct values differ by six cycles, so expression is not equal.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The normal tissue has the higher Ct (25), which corresponds to lower, not higher, expression.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A lower Ct in the tumor indicates a higher, not lower, initial concentration of target.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A lower Ct means fewer cycles were needed for the tumor sample, not more.

questions.topicName: Molecular Biology Techniques (3 of 3), RNA analysis

questions.stem: During a qPCR run, one sample's fluorescence crosses the detection threshold after only a small number of cycles (a low Ct). What does this most directly indicate about the target in that sample?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A high initial target concentration

choices.label: B
choices.text: A low initial target concentration

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reverse transcription of the RNA failed

choices.label: D
choices.text: The gene is poorly expressed

choices.label: E
choices.text: The target is absent from the sample

explanation.summary: Low Ct equals fewer cycles needed, reflecting abundant starting target and high expression.
explanation.whyCorrect: Because Ct is inversely proportional to the amount of starting target, a low Ct means fewer cycles were required to exceed background, which reflects a high initial concentration of target and thus a highly expressed gene.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A low initial concentration would require more cycles and give a high Ct.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Failed reverse transcription would leave little or no cDNA to amplify, yielding a high or undetectable Ct, not a low one.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A poorly expressed gene starts with little target and produces a high Ct.
whyWrongByChoice.E: An absent target would not cross the threshold or would give a very high/undetermined Ct.

questions.topicName: Molecular Biology Techniques (3 of 3), RNA analysis

questions.stem: A clinician monitors an HIV-infected patient's viral load, which is reported as the number of copies of HIV RNA per milliliter of plasma. The value is obtained by comparing the sample's Ct to a curve built from serial dilutions of a template of known concentration. Which quantification approach does this describe?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Absolute quantification

choices.label: B
choices.text: Differential expression analysis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Endpoint RT-PCR

choices.label: D
choices.text: Fold-change analysis between two conditions

choices.label: E
choices.text: Relative (semi-quantitative) quantification

explanation.summary: Reporting exact copies/mL against a standard curve is absolute quantification.
explanation.whyCorrect: Absolute quantification provides the exact concentration (number of molecules) of a target by interpolating the sample's Ct on a standard curve generated from serial dilutions of a known reference. HIV viral load, reported as copies per milliliter of plasma, is a classic example.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Differential expression analysis is a downstream step in RNA-seq, not a plasma viral-load assay.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Endpoint RT-PCR only confirms presence of a product and is not quantitative.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Fold-change analysis is the output of relative quantification, not an absolute copies/mL measurement.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Relative quantification compares Ct values across conditions to estimate fold change; it does not yield an absolute copy number.

questions.topicName: Molecular Biology Techniques (3 of 3), RNA analysis

questions.stem: The first step of RT-qPCR is generating a DNA copy from extracted RNA. Which enzyme, originally derived from retroviruses such as HIV-1, carries out this conversion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: DNA ligase

choices.label: B
choices.text: Restriction endonuclease

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reverse transcriptase

choices.label: D
choices.text: RNA polymerase II

choices.label: E
choices.text: Taq polymerase

explanation.summary: Reverse transcriptase synthesizes cDNA from an RNA template.
explanation.whyCorrect: Reverse transcriptase, obtained from retroviruses like HIV-1, converts extracted RNA into complementary DNA (cDNA). This cDNA then serves as the template for amplification in RT-qPCR.

whyWrongByChoice.A: DNA ligase joins DNA fragments and has no role in RNA-to-DNA conversion.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Restriction endonucleases cut DNA at specific sequences and do not synthesize cDNA.
whyWrongByChoice.D: RNA polymerase II synthesizes RNA from a DNA template, the opposite direction.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Taq polymerase amplifies DNA during the cycling steps; it does not make DNA from RNA.

questions.topicName: Molecular Biology Techniques (3 of 3), RNA analysis

questions.stem: To perform absolute quantification, a laboratory runs serial dilutions of a template of known concentration and builds a standard curve. How is this standard curve typically constructed?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ct values on the y-axis against the log10 of the known concentrations on the x-axis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ct values on the y-axis against the melting temperature of each amplicon on the x-axis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fluorescence intensity on the y-axis against elapsed reaction time on the x-axis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Known concentration on the y-axis against raw fluorescence intensity on the x-axis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Number of sequencing reads on the y-axis against gene length on the x-axis

explanation.summary: The qPCR standard curve plots Ct (y) versus log10 concentration (x) with a linear fit.
explanation.whyCorrect: A standard curve is made by plotting the log10 of the known concentrations on the x-axis and the corresponding Ct values on the y-axis, then fitting a linear regression line. Unknown samples are quantified by interpolating their Ct on this line.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Ct versus melting temperature describes melt-curve (specificity) analysis, not the quantification standard curve.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fluorescence versus time describes a single amplification trace, not the standard curve used for quantification.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The axes are reversed and there is no log transform of concentration; the curve uses Ct versus log10 concentration.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Reads versus gene length relates to RNA-seq normalization, not to a qPCR standard curve.

questions.topicName: Molecular Biology Techniques (3 of 3), RNA analysis

questions.stem: Researchers want to characterize the diverse immune, stromal, and malignant cell populations within a single tumor and to detect rare T-cell and macrophage subtypes that would be averaged out by pooled-tissue methods. Which technique is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bulk tissue RNA sequencing

choices.label: B
choices.text: RT-qPCR of tumor lysate

choices.label: C
choices.text: Single-cell RNA sequencing

choices.label: D
choices.text: Southern blot of tumor DNA

choices.label: E
choices.text: Western blot of tumor lysate

explanation.summary: Single-cell RNA-seq resolves distinct and rare cell populations within heterogeneous tissue.
explanation.whyCorrect: Single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) profiles the transcriptome of individual cells, allowing identification of distinct cell populations and gene-expression clusters. It can uncover rare subtypes in the tumor microenvironment that bulk methods miss because of averaging effects.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bulk RNA-seq averages signal across all cells, obscuring rare subpopulations.
whyWrongByChoice.B: RT-qPCR quantifies known genes in a bulk lysate and cannot resolve individual cell types.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Southern blot detects DNA sequences and has no role in single-cell expression profiling.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Western blot measures protein abundance, not single-cell transcriptomes.

questions.topicName: Molecular Biology Techniques (3 of 3), RNA analysis

questions.stem: An RNA-seq experiment flags a low-abundance transcript as differentially expressed. The team now needs to validate this specific gene with a highly sensitive, precise, targeted assay. Which method is best suited for the validation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A heatmap

choices.label: B
choices.text: A volcano plot

choices.label: C
choices.text: Repeating bulk RNA sequencing

choices.label: D
choices.text: RT-qPCR

choices.label: E
choices.text: Single-cell RNA sequencing

explanation.summary: RT-qPCR is the targeted, high-sensitivity method used to validate specific RNA-seq hits.
explanation.whyCorrect: RT-qPCR has very high sensitivity for low-abundance transcripts and high precision from specific primer design, making it the standard tool to validate a particular gene identified by broader transcriptomic analyses such as RNA-seq.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A heatmap is a way to display expression data, not a method to validate a transcript.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A volcano plot is a visualization of differential expression, not a laboratory assay.
whyWrongByChoice.C: RNA-seq has only moderate sensitivity and may miss low-expression genes, so repeating it does not add the precision needed for validation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: scRNA-seq resolves cell types but is still a sequencing approach with lower per-gene sensitivity than qPCR and is not a targeted validation assay.

questions.topicName: Molecular Biology Techniques (3 of 3), RNA analysis

questions.stem: RNA-seq is commonly used to study the effects of treatments or mutations on gene expression and to detect gene fusions in cancer. Which of the following is NOT an appropriate use of RNA-seq?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Analyzing the effect of a drug treatment on gene expression

choices.label: B
choices.text: Comparing expression between wild-type and mutant organisms

choices.label: C
choices.text: Detecting gene fusions in cancer

choices.label: D
choices.text: Discovering novel dysregulated genes across conditions

choices.label: E
choices.text: Identifying a specific germline point mutation

explanation.summary: Identifying a point mutation is a DNA-sequencing task, not a primary use of RNA-seq.
explanation.whyCorrect: RNA-seq measures the transcriptome to assess expression changes and detect gene fusions, but it is not the primary method for identifying specific point mutations; DNA sequencing is used to detect mutations directly.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Analyzing the effect of a treatment on expression is a standard RNA-seq application.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Comparing wild-type versus mutant expression is a listed use of RNA-seq.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Detecting gene fusions, especially in cancer, is a recognized strength of RNA-seq.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Discovering novel dysregulated genes across conditions is a core exploratory use of RNA-seq.

questions.topicName: Molecular Biology Techniques (3 of 3), RNA analysis

questions.stem: Which single feature most distinguishes quantitative real-time PCR (qPCR) from conventional endpoint PCR?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Fluorescence is measured at every cycle

choices.label: B
choices.text: It does not require primers to define the target sequence

choices.label: C
choices.text: It does not require Taq polymerase

choices.label: D
choices.text: It sequences the entire transcriptome in a single reaction

choices.label: E
choices.text: It uses reverse transcriptase, which conventional PCR can never use

explanation.summary: Real-time fluorescence measurement each cycle is the defining feature of qPCR.
explanation.whyCorrect: qPCR shares most components with conventional PCR (Taq polymerase, primers, dNTPs, template) but adds a fluorescent compound whose signal is measured at each cycle. This real-time readout allows the amount of DNA to be quantified as it accumulates, which conventional endpoint PCR cannot do.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Both qPCR and conventional PCR require primers to define the target sequence.
whyWrongByChoice.C: qPCR still relies on Taq polymerase for amplification.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Transcriptome-wide sequencing describes RNA-seq, not qPCR.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Reverse transcription is a separate upstream step; conventional PCR can also be preceded by reverse transcription (RT-PCR), so RT is not the distinguishing feature.

questions.topicName: Molecular Biology Techniques (3 of 3), RNA analysis

questions.stem: A laboratory assesses breast cancer recurrence risk by measuring the expression levels of specific genes such as Ki-67 and by quantifying circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA). Which technique provides the precise, targeted quantification described here?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bulk RNA sequencing

choices.label: B
choices.text: Karyotyping

choices.label: C
choices.text: qPCR (RT-qPCR)

choices.label: D
choices.text: Single-cell RNA sequencing

choices.label: E
choices.text: Western blot

explanation.summary: qPCR provides precise, targeted quantification of defined markers such as Ki-67 expression and ctDNA.
explanation.whyCorrect: qPCR is used in cancer diagnostics to quantify predictive markers, including expression levels of specific genes like Ki-67 and circulating tumor DNA, to estimate the likelihood of recurrence in patients with breast cancer. Its specificity and sensitivity make it suited to measuring these predefined targets.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bulk RNA-seq is a global exploratory method and is not the targeted, precise assay used for these specific recurrence markers.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Karyotyping visualizes whole chromosomes and cannot quantify gene expression or ctDNA levels.
whyWrongByChoice.D: scRNA-seq profiles individual cells and is not used for routine quantification of these markers.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Western blot detects protein by antibody but does not quantify ctDNA or provide the targeted nucleic-acid quantification described.

questions.topicName: Molecular Biology Techniques (3 of 3), RNA analysis

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman presents with fever and cough during a respiratory virus outbreak. A nasal swab is sent for real-time PCR testing for SARS-CoV-2. The laboratory protocol for this virus includes an initial reverse-transcription step that is absent from its protocol for a pathogen whose genetic material is DNA. Which feature of the pathogen best explains the need for this additional step?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Nasal swab material quenches the fluorescent signal unless it is pretreated

choices.label: B
choices.text: The detected target is a viral capsid protein rather than a nucleic acid

choices.label: C
choices.text: The viral genome is RNA and must be converted to cDNA before amplification

choices.label: D
choices.text: The virus encodes a polymerase that competes with Taq polymerase during cycling

choices.label: E
choices.text: The virus is present at extremely high copy number in nasal secretions

explanation.summary: RT-PCR detects RNA (viral or cellular) by first converting it to cDNA, which then serves as the template for amplification.
explanation.whyCorrect: RT-PCR is used to detect RNA molecules, especially from viruses or genes expressed in cells. RNA is extracted from a sample such as a nasal swab and converted into complementary DNA by reverse transcriptase; this cDNA is the template that Taq polymerase amplifies. A DNA-genome pathogen already provides a DNA template, so no reverse-transcription step is needed.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The extra step converts RNA to cDNA; it is not a pretreatment to protect the fluorescent readout.
whyWrongByChoice.B: qPCR detects nucleic acid; a protein target would call for a protein-based assay, not reverse transcription.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The need for reverse transcription reflects the RNA nature of the template, not competition from a viral polymerase.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Copy number affects the Ct value, not whether a reverse-transcription step is required.

questions.topicName: Molecular Biology Techniques (3 of 3), RNA analysis

questions.stem: The enzyme used to generate cDNA in RT-PCR was originally isolated from retroviruses, which depend on it for their replication. Which of the following human viruses is a retrovirus associated with the development of certain leukemias and neurological diseases?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Hepatitis B and hepatitis C viruses

choices.label: B
choices.text: Human immunodeficiency virus type 1

choices.label: C
choices.text: Human T-lymphotropic virus type 1

choices.label: D
choices.text: Influenza A virus (orthomyxovirus)

choices.label: E
choices.text: SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19 coronavirus)

explanation.summary: HTLV-1 and HTLV-II are retroviruses linked to certain leukemias and neurological diseases.
explanation.whyCorrect: Reverse transcriptase is crucial for retrovirus replication. The most well-known human retroviruses are HIV and human T-lymphotropic virus (HTLV). HTLV has two types, HTLV-1 and HTLV-II, which can lead to certain types of leukemia and neurological diseases.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Hepatitis viruses are tested for by qPCR but are not the retroviruses associated with leukemia described here.
whyWrongByChoice.B: HIV is a retrovirus that relies on reverse transcriptase, but it causes AIDS rather than the leukemias and neurological diseases attributed to HTLV.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Influenza is detected by qPCR in infectious disease diagnosis, but it is not a retrovirus.
whyWrongByChoice.E: SARS-CoV-2 is an RNA virus diagnosed by qPCR, but it is not a retrovirus and is not associated with leukemia.

questions.topicName: Molecular Biology Techniques (3 of 3), RNA analysis

questions.stem: A technician assembles a reaction containing Taq polymerase, gene-specific primers, dNTPs and cDNA template, then runs it on a real-time thermocycler. No amplification curve is displayed during the run, yet gel electrophoresis of the finished reaction shows a product of the expected size. Which reagent was most likely omitted?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A fluorescent compound

choices.label: B
choices.text: Deoxynucleotide triphosphates (dNTPs)

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gene-specific primers

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reverse transcriptase

choices.label: E
choices.text: Taq polymerase

explanation.summary: qPCR uses the same components as conventional PCR plus a fluorescent compound that reports amplification in real time.
explanation.whyCorrect: The components of a qPCR reaction are very similar to conventional PCR: Taq polymerase, primers to define the target, dNTPs and the cDNA template. In addition, qPCR requires a fluorescent compound so that fluorescence can be measured at each cycle. Without it, amplification still occurs (hence the gel band) but no real-time signal is produced.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Without dNTPs no new DNA strands could be synthesized, so no product would appear.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Without primers to define the target sequence, no specific product could have been generated.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Reverse transcriptase acts upstream to make cDNA; the reaction already contained cDNA template, so its absence would not explain a silent run that still yields product.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Without Taq polymerase there would be no amplification and therefore no product on the gel.

questions.topicName: Molecular Biology Techniques (3 of 3), RNA analysis

questions.stem: A graduate student performs RT-qPCR on RNA from a single liver biopsy using primer sets for two different genes. Gene A gives a Ct of 18 and gene B gives a Ct of 26. The student concludes that gene A is expressed at higher levels than gene B in the liver. Which of the following is the most appropriate response to this conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A higher Ct indicates the more highly expressed gene, so the conclusion is reversed

choices.label: B
choices.text: A lower Ct always reflects a more abundant transcript, so the conclusion is valid

choices.label: C
choices.text: A standard curve must be generated before any Ct values can be compared

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ct comparison applies to one gene across conditions, not to two different genes

choices.label: E
choices.text: Gene expression cannot be measured by qPCR in tissue obtained by biopsy

explanation.summary: qPCR quantifies expression of ONE gene across different conditions; it does not compare the expression of two different genes.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ct values are interpreted by comparing the same target gene between conditions (if CtA < CtB, gene X is more expressed in condition A than in condition B). qPCR does not compare the expression of two different genes, so contrasting gene A's Ct with gene B's Ct within one sample is not a valid use of the method.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A higher Ct means more cycles were needed and a lower initial amount, so this reverses the Ct relationship in addition to making the same invalid cross-gene comparison.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Low Ct does reflect abundant target for a given gene, but the comparison here is between two different genes, which qPCR is not designed to make.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A standard curve is needed for absolute quantification; relative comparisons of a single gene across conditions do not require one, and a curve would not fix a cross-gene comparison.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Biopsies are a listed sample type from which RNA is extracted for RT-PCR.

questions.topicName: Molecular Biology Techniques (3 of 3), RNA analysis

questions.stem: A laboratory report from a real-time PCR run lists a Ct value for each sample. Which of the following best defines this value?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The fluorescence intensity measured at the plateau of the reaction

choices.label: B
choices.text: The number of copies of target present at the end of the final cycle

choices.label: C
choices.text: The number of cycles required for the fluorescent signal to exceed background

choices.label: D
choices.text: The temperature at which the double-stranded amplicon separates

choices.label: E
choices.text: The total number of amplification cycles programmed on the thermocycler

explanation.summary: Ct (cycle threshold) is the cycle number at which fluorescence crosses the threshold above background.
explanation.whyCorrect: The Ct, or cycle threshold, is the number of cycles required for the fluorescence signal to exceed the background level. Because fluorescence grows exponentially with the amount of DNA, the cycle at which the signal crosses the threshold reflects how much target was present initially.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ct is read where the signal crosses the threshold during the rise, not at the plateau.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Ct is a cycle number, not a copy count at the end of the run; copy number is derived from Ct via a standard curve.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The temperature at which strands separate relates to the denaturation step, not to the Ct.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The programmed number of cycles is fixed for the run and is not the Ct.

questions.topicName: Molecular Biology Techniques (3 of 3), RNA analysis

questions.stem: A technician prepares serial 10-fold dilutions of a reference template (1000, 100, 10, 1 and 0.1 ng/µL), runs qPCR on each, and fits a linear regression of Ct against log10 concentration. Which of the following best describes the resulting line?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ct falls linearly as log10 concentration increases

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ct falls only once concentration exceeds 100 ng/µL

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ct is constant across concentrations when conditions are identical

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ct rises exponentially as log10 concentration increases

choices.label: E
choices.text: Ct rises linearly as log10 concentration increases

explanation.summary: Because Ct is inversely proportional to starting template, the standard curve is a straight line with a negative slope.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ct is inversely proportional to the initial amount of target: more template means fewer cycles are needed to cross the threshold. When Ct is plotted on the y-axis against log10 of the known concentrations on the x-axis, the fitted regression line therefore slopes downward, with the most concentrated standard having the lowest Ct.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Ct decreases across the whole dilution series, not only above a particular concentration.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Identical conditions are required for validity, but Ct still changes with template amount; a flat line would make quantification impossible.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The curve is a linear fit of Ct versus log10 concentration, not an exponential rise.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A rising line would mean more template needs more cycles, the opposite of the inverse relationship.

questions.topicName: Molecular Biology Techniques (3 of 3), RNA analysis

questions.stem: A qPCR standard curve built from serial dilutions of a known template gives Ct values of 27, 24, 21, 18 and 15 for 0.1, 1, 10, 100 and 1000 ng/µL, respectively. An unknown sample run under identical conditions gives a Ct of 22. Which of the following is the best estimate of the sample's template concentration?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Between 0.1 and 1 ng/µL

choices.label: B
choices.text: Between 1 and 10 ng/µL

choices.label: C
choices.text: Between 10 and 100 ng/µL

choices.label: D
choices.text: Greater than 1000 ng/µL

choices.label: E
choices.text: Less than 0.1 ng/µL

explanation.summary: Unknowns are quantified by interpolating their Ct on the standard curve; a Ct between two standards places the concentration between those standards.
explanation.whyCorrect: Absolute quantification interpolates an unknown's Ct on the regression line of Ct versus log10 concentration. A Ct of 22 falls between the Ct of the 10 ng/µL standard (21) and the 1 ng/µL standard (24). Because Ct decreases as concentration increases, the sample must contain between 1 and 10 ng/µL of template.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Concentrations between 0.1 and 1 ng/µL correspond to Ct values between 27 and 24, higher than the observed 22.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Concentrations between 10 and 100 ng/µL correspond to Ct values between 21 and 18, lower than 22.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A concentration above 1000 ng/µL would give a Ct below 15.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A concentration below 0.1 ng/µL would give a Ct greater than 27.

questions.topicName: Molecular Biology Techniques (3 of 3), RNA analysis

questions.stem: A laboratory generates a standard curve for HIV RNA quantification on Monday. On Wednesday, patient plasma samples are run using a different thermocycler program and a new lot of fluorescent reagent, and their Ct values are interpolated on Monday's curve. The reported copies per milliliter are most likely unreliable for which of the following reasons?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Absolute quantification cannot be applied to viral RNA targets

choices.label: B
choices.text: HIV viral load can be expressed only as a fold change

choices.label: C
choices.text: Serial dilutions are valid only when prepared in patient plasma

choices.label: D
choices.text: The standard curve must be plotted with Ct on the x-axis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Unknown samples must be run under the same conditions as the standards

explanation.summary: Absolute quantification requires that all samples, standards and unknowns, be run under identical conditions.
explanation.whyCorrect: Absolute quantification relies on a standard curve from a reference sample of known concentration, and all samples must be run under identical conditions so that the Ct of an unknown can be validly interpolated on that curve. Changing the cycling program and reagent lot between the standards and the unknowns breaks this requirement.

whyWrongByChoice.A: HIV viral load in plasma is a classic absolute quantification reported as copies per milliliter.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Fold change is the output of relative quantification; viral load is reported as an absolute copy number.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The standard curve is made from serial dilutions of a known template; the diluent is not the issue described.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The standard curve places log10 concentration on the x-axis and Ct on the y-axis; the axis choice is not the problem here.

questions.topicName: Molecular Biology Techniques (3 of 3), RNA analysis

questions.stem: A research group treats cultured cells with a candidate drug and wants to know how many times higher the expression of gene X is in treated cells compared with untreated cells. They do not need the exact number of transcript molecules. Which of the following approaches is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Absolute quantification with a standard curve of known template

choices.label: B
choices.text: Endpoint PCR followed by gel electrophoresis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Northern blot of treated and untreated cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: Relative quantification comparing Ct values between conditions

choices.label: E
choices.text: Single-cell RNA sequencing of treated and untreated cells

explanation.summary: Relative (semi-quantitative) qPCR compares Ct values across conditions to calculate fold change without needing exact transcript counts.
explanation.whyCorrect: Relative quantification compares the Ct values of a target gene across experimental conditions to calculate fold change, that is, how much more or less gene X is expressed in condition A than in condition B. It is widely used in research settings because the exact amount of transcript is not necessarily required.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Absolute quantification gives the exact concentration of target, which the group does not need and which requires a standard curve.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Endpoint PCR only confirms the presence of a product; it does not quantify expression.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Northern blot detects RNA but is not a quantitative method.
whyWrongByChoice.E: scRNA-seq resolves individual cell populations and is not the targeted tool for a fold change of one known gene.

questions.topicName: Molecular Biology Techniques (3 of 3), RNA analysis

questions.stem: A carcinoma cell line is exposed to increasing concentrations of a compound for 72 hours, and mRNA expression of a target gene is then measured by qPCR. The results are graphed with the 0 µM sample set to 1.0 and the highest dose reaching about 2.0. Which of the following best describes the value of 2.0?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Expression at the highest dose is about twice that of untreated cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: The highest dose required two more cycles to cross the threshold

choices.label: C
choices.text: The target concentration at the highest dose is 2.0 ng/µL

choices.label: D
choices.text: There are two copies of the target transcript per cell at the highest dose

choices.label: E
choices.text: Two of the tested doses produced a significant change in expression

explanation.summary: Relative expression graphs report fold change against a reference condition, not absolute copy numbers.
explanation.whyCorrect: Relative quantification calculates fold change, how much more or less a gene is expressed in one condition compared with another. Normalizing the untreated sample to 1.0 makes each treated value a fold change relative to it, so 2.0 indicates roughly twofold higher expression at the highest dose.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Higher expression means fewer cycles to cross the threshold, and the y-axis shows relative expression, not Ct.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A concentration in ng/µL is an absolute quantity that requires a standard curve; this graph reports relative expression.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Copies per cell would come from absolute quantification with a standard curve, not from a relative expression plot.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The value 2.0 describes the magnitude of expression change, not the number of doses that were significant.

questions.topicName: Molecular Biology Techniques (3 of 3), RNA analysis

questions.stem: A researcher wants to measure the expression of approximately 5,000 genes in three tissue samples in a single experiment. A colleague advises against using RT-qPCR for this project. Which feature of RT-qPCR best supports this advice?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It cannot be performed on RNA extracted from tissue

choices.label: B
choices.text: Its cost per gene exceeds that of sequencing for small gene sets

choices.label: C
choices.text: Its precision is poor because primers bind nonspecifically

choices.label: D
choices.text: Its sensitivity is too low to detect most transcripts

choices.label: E
choices.text: Its throughput is low, limited to a few genes per run

explanation.summary: RT-qPCR has low throughput (a few genes per run), whereas RNA-seq analyzes thousands of genes simultaneously.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the comparison of the two methods, RT-qPCR throughput is low and limited to a few genes per run, while RNA-seq throughput is high, with thousands of genes analyzed simultaneously. Measuring thousands of genes is therefore a job for RNA-seq.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Biopsies and tissues are standard sources of RNA for RT-PCR.
whyWrongByChoice.B: RT-qPCR cost is relatively low for small gene sets; the problem is scale, not cost per gene.
whyWrongByChoice.C: RT-qPCR precision is high because of specific primer design.
whyWrongByChoice.D: RT-qPCR sensitivity is very high; it can detect low-abundance transcripts.

questions.topicName: Molecular Biology Techniques (3 of 3), RNA analysis

questions.stem: A small laboratory with a limited budget needs to quantify three well-characterized genes in 40 patient samples. Which of the following approaches is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bulk RNA sequencing with deep coverage of every sample

choices.label: B
choices.text: Northern blot with probes for the three genes

choices.label: C
choices.text: RT-qPCR with primers for the three genes

choices.label: D
choices.text: Single-cell RNA sequencing of each patient sample

choices.label: E
choices.text: Western blot of each sample for the three genes

explanation.summary: For a small set of known genes, RT-qPCR is precise, targeted and relatively low in cost.
explanation.whyCorrect: RT-qPCR is ideal for precise, targeted quantification of known genes, and its cost is relatively low for small gene sets. RNA-seq cost is higher, especially for deep sequencing or many samples, so a targeted three-gene panel across 40 samples is best handled by qPCR.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Deep sequencing of many samples is the highest-cost scenario for RNA-seq and is unnecessary for three known genes.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Northern blot detects RNA but is not a quantitative method.
whyWrongByChoice.D: scRNA-seq is a sequencing approach for resolving cell populations, not an economical way to quantify three known genes in many samples.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Western blot measures protein, not gene expression at the transcript level.

questions.topicName: Molecular Biology Techniques (3 of 3), RNA analysis

questions.stem: Two groups measure expression of the same gene in identical samples. Group 1 uses RT-qPCR and Group 2 uses RNA-seq. Group 2's replicate values vary more widely than Group 1's. Which of the following best explains the lower precision of the RNA-seq measurements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: RNA-seq cannot be applied to the same tissue types as qPCR

choices.label: B
choices.text: RNA-seq measures fluorescence only at the end of the run

choices.label: C
choices.text: RNA-seq omits the reverse-transcription step used in qPCR

choices.label: D
choices.text: RNA-seq quantification depends on sequencing depth and alignment accuracy

choices.label: E
choices.text: RNA-seq requires prior knowledge of the gene for primer design

explanation.summary: RT-qPCR precision is high because of specific primer design; RNA-seq precision is lower and depends on sequencing depth and alignment accuracy.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the comparison of the two methods, RT-qPCR precision is high due to specific primer design, whereas RNA-seq precision is lower because it depends on sequencing depth and alignment accuracy. Technical limitations such as depth and coverage explain the greater variability of RNA-seq quantification.

whyWrongByChoice.A: RNA-seq is performed on the same kinds of biological samples (cell lines, tissues) as qPCR.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Per-cycle fluorescence measurement is a feature of qPCR; RNA-seq is a sequencing method, not a fluorescence-cycle assay.
whyWrongByChoice.C: RNA-seq also reverse-transcribes extracted RNA into cDNA before sequencing.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Prior knowledge of target genes is a limitation of qPCR, not RNA-seq, which is exploratory.

questions.topicName: Molecular Biology Techniques (3 of 3), RNA analysis

questions.stem: A gene known from prior RT-qPCR work to be expressed at low levels in kidney is not detected in a bulk RNA-seq dataset generated from the same tissue. Which of the following is the most likely explanation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Limits in sequencing depth and coverage caused the low-abundance transcript to be missed

choices.label: B
choices.text: RNA-seq detects only transcripts that are upregulated relative to a control

choices.label: C
choices.text: RT-qPCR produced a false-positive signal because it relies on Taq polymerase

choices.label: D
choices.text: The gene lies in a genomic region that cannot be reverse transcribed

choices.label: E
choices.text: The transcript was degraded during a reverse-transcription step unique to RNA-seq

explanation.summary: Because of technical limitations like sequencing depth and coverage, RNA-seq may miss low-expression genes that qPCR can detect.
explanation.whyCorrect: RNA-seq sensitivity is moderate: low-expression genes may be missed because of coverage limits, and its listed limitation is that it may miss low-expression or poorly annotated genes. RT-qPCR, by contrast, has very high sensitivity and can detect low-abundance transcripts.

whyWrongByChoice.B: RNA-seq surveys the whole transcriptome and identifies both up- and downregulated genes; it is not restricted to upregulated transcripts.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Taq polymerase is used in both conventional PCR and qPCR and does not make qPCR a false-positive-prone method.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Both methods reverse-transcribe the same extracted RNA; a gene qPCR detects was clearly reverse transcribed.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Reverse transcription to cDNA is part of both RNA-seq and RT-qPCR, not unique to RNA-seq.

questions.topicName: Molecular Biology Techniques (3 of 3), RNA analysis

questions.stem: RNA-seq is described as a method for studying the transcriptome. Which of the following best defines the transcriptome?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The collection of all gene fusions present in a tumor sample at diagnosis

choices.label: B
choices.text: The complete set of proteins produced by a cell throughout its entire lifetime

choices.label: C
choices.text: The complete set of RNA transcripts present in a sample at a specific time

choices.label: D
choices.text: The full DNA sequence of an organism's genome in every one of its cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: The set of DNA sequences bound by transcription factors in a given cell

explanation.summary: The transcriptome is the complete set of RNA transcripts in a biological sample at a specific time.
explanation.whyCorrect: RNA-seq uses next-generation sequencing to study the transcriptome, defined as the complete set of RNA transcripts present in a biological sample (such as a cell line or tissue) at a specific time. This allows gene expression patterns to be analyzed across conditions, individuals or tissue types.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Gene fusions can be detected by RNA-seq, but they are only one feature, not the definition of the transcriptome.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The set of proteins is studied by proteomic approaches such as LC-MS/MS, not by RNA-seq.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The genome is DNA; the transcriptome is the RNA that is transcribed from it at a given time.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Protein-DNA binding sites are identified by ChIP-seq, not defined as the transcriptome.

questions.topicName: Molecular Biology Techniques (3 of 3), RNA analysis

questions.stem: A laboratory performs both RT-qPCR and bulk RNA-seq on RNA extracted from the same biopsy. Which of the following steps is common to both workflows?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Construction of a standard curve from serial dilutions

choices.label: B
choices.text: Design of primers specific to the gene of interest

choices.label: C
choices.text: Measurement of fluorescence during each amplification cycle

choices.label: D
choices.text: Next-generation sequencing of the prepared material

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reverse transcription of the RNA into cDNA

explanation.summary: Both RT-qPCR and RNA-seq begin by reverse-transcribing extracted RNA into cDNA.
explanation.whyCorrect: In RNA-seq, RNAs are extracted from the biological samples and reverse-transcribed into cDNA before NGS is performed and the data analyzed. RT-qPCR likewise begins with RNA extraction and conversion to cDNA by reverse transcriptase before amplification. The reverse-transcription step is therefore shared.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A standard curve is used for absolute quantification in qPCR, not in RNA-seq.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Gene-specific primer design makes qPCR targeted; RNA-seq is a global method that does not require primers for a gene of interest.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Per-cycle fluorescence measurement is the defining feature of qPCR and is not part of RNA-seq.
whyWrongByChoice.D: NGS is the readout for RNA-seq only; qPCR quantifies by fluorescence, not sequencing.

questions.topicName: Molecular Biology Techniques (3 of 3), RNA analysis

questions.stem: An RNA-seq comparison of tumor and healthy tissue produces a spreadsheet listing several thousand significantly up- or downregulated genes. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in interpreting these data?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Apply analysis tools to identify the pathways and protein networks affected

choices.label: B
choices.text: Discard the genes with the largest fold changes as probable sequencing artifacts

choices.label: C
choices.text: Repeat the sequencing runs until fewer genes appear on the final list

choices.label: D
choices.text: Treat every listed gene as biologically relevant to the tumor's behavior

choices.label: E
choices.text: Validate all of the listed genes individually with RT-qPCR assays

explanation.summary: RNA-seq yields thousands of dysregulated genes, not all relevant; dedicated tools are used to decipher which gene, pathway or protein network is impacted.
explanation.whyCorrect: RNA-seq results are often displayed in large files containing thousands of lines. RNA-seq identifies thousands of dysregulated genes, but they are not all relevant, so the datasheet must be analyzed. Different tools have been developed to read between the lines and decipher which gene, pathway or protein network is impacted.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Large fold changes are exactly the differentially expressed genes of interest; there is no basis for discarding them.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A long list is expected from a transcriptome-wide method; repeating the run does not replace analysis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Not all dysregulated genes are relevant; treating them all as meaningful ignores the need for analysis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: qPCR is low throughput (a few genes per run) and is used to validate selected hits, not thousands of genes.

questions.topicName: Molecular Biology Techniques (3 of 3), RNA analysis

questions.stem: A figure from a transcriptome sequencing study of calcified aortic valve disease plots each gene as a single point, with log fold change on the x-axis and the negative log10 of the p-value on the y-axis; significantly upregulated genes cluster on the right and downregulated genes on the left. Which of the following is this type of plot?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amplification curve

choices.label: B
choices.text: Heatmap

choices.label: C
choices.text: Principal component analysis plot

choices.label: D
choices.text: Standard curve

choices.label: E
choices.text: Volcano plot

explanation.summary: A volcano plot displays differentially expressed genes by fold change against statistical significance.
explanation.whyCorrect: Differentially expressed genes from RNA-seq are visualized with plots such as the volcano plot and the heatmap. The volcano plot places log fold change on the x-axis and -log10(p-value) on the y-axis, so significantly up- and downregulated genes separate to the right and left.

whyWrongByChoice.A: An amplification curve shows fluorescence rising across qPCR cycles.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A heatmap shows expression levels of many genes across samples as a color-coded grid, not individual points on fold-change axes.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A PCA plot positions whole samples (individuals) by principal components, not single genes by fold change and p-value.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A standard curve plots Ct against log10 concentration for absolute quantification in qPCR.

questions.topicName: Molecular Biology Techniques (3 of 3), RNA analysis

questions.stem: A researcher wants to display the expression levels of several hundred differentially expressed genes across all control and disease samples in one color-coded grid, with the samples grouped by condition. Which of the following visualizations is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amplification plot of fluorescence versus cycle

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bar graph of a single gene's fold change

choices.label: C
choices.text: Heatmap

choices.label: D
choices.text: Standard curve

choices.label: E
choices.text: Volcano plot

explanation.summary: A heatmap presents expression of many genes across many samples as a color-coded matrix.
explanation.whyCorrect: Heatmaps are one of the standard ways to observe differentially expressed genes from RNA-seq. Each row is a gene and each column a sample, with color indicating expression level and samples grouped by condition (for example, control versus disease), so hundreds of genes can be surveyed at once.

whyWrongByChoice.A: An amplification plot tracks fluorescence per cycle for a qPCR reaction, not hundreds of genes.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A bar graph of one gene's fold change is the typical qPCR display and cannot show hundreds of genes.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A standard curve is a qPCR tool for absolute quantification, not a display of transcriptome data.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A volcano plot shows each gene's fold change against significance, not expression across individual samples.

questions.topicName: Molecular Biology Techniques (3 of 3), RNA analysis

questions.stem: DNA sequencing of a patient's tumor identifies a mutation in a signaling gene. The oncology team wants to know whether the mutation has altered splicing of that gene's transcript and whether expression of genes downstream in the same cascade has changed. Which of the following is the most appropriate technique?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Karyotyping

choices.label: B
choices.text: Repeat DNA sequencing at greater depth

choices.label: C
choices.text: RNA sequencing

choices.label: D
choices.text: RT-qPCR of the mutated gene alone

choices.label: E
choices.text: Western blot of the mutated protein

explanation.summary: RNA-seq complements DNA sequencing by revealing splice variants and expression changes in cascades downstream of identified mutations.
explanation.whyCorrect: RNA-seq offers clinical utility in cancer molecular diagnostics by complementing DNA sequencing in identifying gene fusions, splice variants and expression changes. It is particularly useful where DNA-based tests are insufficient, such as analyzing alterations of gene expression in cascades downstream of identified mutations.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Karyotyping visualizes chromosomes and cannot detect splicing or expression alterations.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The mutation is already identified; deeper DNA sequencing does not reveal splicing or downstream expression changes, which occur at the RNA level.
whyWrongByChoice.D: RT-qPCR quantifies one known gene and does not characterize splice variants or survey a downstream cascade.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Western blot measures a single protein and cannot address transcript splicing or a cascade of expression changes.

questions.topicName: Molecular Biology Techniques (3 of 3), RNA analysis

questions.stem: Developmental biologists studying organogenesis want to map how stem cells in a highly heterogeneous embryonic tissue differentiate into specialized cell types and to identify the transcriptional programs guiding these cell-fate decisions. Which of the following is the most appropriate technique?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Absolute qPCR with a standard curve of reference template

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bulk RNA sequencing of pooled embryonic tissue

choices.label: C
choices.text: Northern blot of RNA from whole embryos

choices.label: D
choices.text: RT-qPCR of a single known lineage marker

choices.label: E
choices.text: Single-cell RNA sequencing across successive embryonic stages

explanation.summary: scRNA-seq reconstructs lineage trajectories in heterogeneous, dynamic embryonic tissue.
explanation.whyCorrect: scRNA-seq has been pivotal in studying embryonic development, where tissues are highly heterogeneous and dynamic. By sequencing individual cells at various stages, researchers reconstruct lineage trajectories, mapping how stem cells differentiate into specialized cell types, which has been used to understand organogenesis and identify transcriptional programs guiding cell-fate decisions.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Absolute qPCR gives the exact concentration of one target; it does not resolve cell populations.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Bulk RNA-seq averages across all cells and would obscure the distinct populations and lineages within heterogeneous tissue.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Northern blot detects a specific RNA in bulk and is not quantitative or cell-resolved.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A single-marker qPCR quantifies one known gene and cannot map lineages or discover transcriptional programs.

questions.topicName: Molecular Biology Techniques (3 of 3), RNA analysis

questions.stem: Which of the following techniques detects a specific RNA molecule but is not a quantitative method?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Northern blot

choices.label: B
choices.text: RNA sequencing

choices.label: C
choices.text: RT-qPCR

choices.label: D
choices.text: Southern blot

choices.label: E
choices.text: Western blot

explanation.summary: Northern blot detects RNA but does not quantify it; RT-qPCR is the quantitative RNA method.
explanation.whyCorrect: Among RNA-analysis methods, RT-qPCR quantifies gene expression by measuring DNA amplification in real time. Northern blot detects RNA, but it is not a quantitative method, so it serves for detection rather than measurement of expression level.

whyWrongByChoice.B: RNA-seq analyzes the transcriptome and reports expression changes across thousands of genes.
whyWrongByChoice.C: RT-qPCR is the quantitative method for RNA, measuring amplification in real time.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Southern blot detects DNA, not RNA.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Western blot detects protein, not RNA.

questions.topicName: Molecular Biology Techniques (3 of 3), RNA analysis

questions.stem: A researcher hypothesizes that a transcription factor regulates a set of genes and wants to identify the DNA sequences to which the factor binds. A colleague suggests RNA-seq. Which of the following techniques is actually suited to this question?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Absolute quantification qPCR

choices.label: B
choices.text: ChIP-seq

choices.label: C
choices.text: LC-MS/MS proteomics

choices.label: D
choices.text: RT-qPCR

choices.label: E
choices.text: Single-cell RNA sequencing

explanation.summary: Identifying DNA sequences where proteins bind to regulate gene expression is a function of ChIP-seq, not RNA-seq.
explanation.whyCorrect: RNA-seq's advantage is studying global expression patterns across the transcriptome. Identifying DNA sequences where proteins bind DNA to regulate gene expression is a different question, answered by ChIP-seq, which analyzes protein interactions with DNA.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Absolute qPCR yields the exact concentration of a nucleic acid target and cannot locate binding sites.
whyWrongByChoice.C: LC-MS/MS is a proteomic approach for studying protein expression, not where a protein binds DNA.
whyWrongByChoice.D: RT-qPCR quantifies expression of known genes; it does not map protein binding sites on DNA.
whyWrongByChoice.E: scRNA-seq profiles transcriptomes of individual cells and does not identify protein-DNA binding sequences.

questions.topicName: Molecular Biology Techniques (3 of 3), RNA analysis

questions.stem: A methods section states that qPCR was used to measure mRNA levels of gene X in treated and untreated cells. Which of the following is implied by this statement even though it is not written?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A Northern blot was performed to confirm the result

choices.label: B
choices.text: The gene's exact copy number per cell was reported

choices.label: C
choices.text: The measurement relied on protein-specific antibodies

choices.label: D
choices.text: The mRNA was first reverse transcribed into cDNA

choices.label: E
choices.text: The mRNA was sequenced by next-generation sequencing

explanation.summary: When qPCR is applied to RNA, the reverse-transcription step (the RT in RT-qPCR) is often implied rather than stated.
explanation.whyCorrect: Real-time PCR is also known as quantitative PCR (qPCR or RT-qPCR), with the RT often implied. Because Taq polymerase amplifies a cDNA template, measuring mRNA by qPCR necessarily means the RNA was first converted to cDNA by reverse transcriptase.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Northern blot is a separate, non-quantitative RNA detection method and is not implied by qPCR.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Comparing treated and untreated cells describes relative quantification (fold change), not an absolute copy number, which would require a standard curve.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Antibody-based detection of protein is Western blot, not qPCR.
whyWrongByChoice.E: NGS is the basis of RNA-seq, not qPCR.

questions.topicName: Molecular Biology Techniques (3 of 3), RNA analysis

questions.stem: A 41-year-old woman presents for her first obstetric visit after a positive home pregnancy test. Her last menstrual period was 6 weeks ago. She is very anxious about her risk of having a child with trisomy 21 and states she wants a definitive answer as early as possible. Which of the following is the most appropriate test to offer once she reaches the earliest window at which it can be performed?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amniocentesis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Anatomy ultrasound

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cell-free DNA testing (NIPT)

choices.label: D
choices.text: Chorionic villus sampling

choices.label: E
choices.text: Maternal serum PAPP-A and beta-hCG

explanation.summary: Chorionic villus sampling is the earliest diagnostic (definitive) prenatal test, performed at 10-14 weeks.
explanation.whyCorrect: CVS is typically performed between 10 and 14 weeks of gestation and directly samples placental (chorionic villus) cells, so it directly examines fetal chromosomes and is diagnostic for trisomies. For a patient who wants a definitive answer at the earliest possible time, CVS is the appropriate choice.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Amniocentesis is also diagnostic but is performed later, at 16-20 weeks, so it is not the earliest option.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Ultrasound can raise suspicion but does not provide a genetic diagnosis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cell-free DNA (NIPT) is a screening test that estimates risk; it is not definitive/diagnostic.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Maternal serum PAPP-A and beta-hCG make up a screening test and cannot confirm a diagnosis.

questions.topicName: Prenatal Genetic Testing & Neonatal Screening

questions.stem: A 32-year-old woman undergoes a second-trimester quadruple screen at 16 weeks of gestation. Which of the following analyte patterns would most likely be reported in a fetus affected by Down syndrome?

choices.label: A
choices.text: MSAFP high, beta-hCG high, estriol high, inhibin A high

choices.label: B
choices.text: MSAFP high, beta-hCG normal, estriol normal, inhibin A normal

choices.label: C
choices.text: MSAFP low, beta-hCG high, estriol low, inhibin A high

choices.label: D
choices.text: MSAFP low, beta-hCG low, estriol low, inhibin A low

choices.label: E
choices.text: MSAFP normal, beta-hCG high, estriol normal, inhibin A normal

explanation.summary: In trisomy 21 the quad screen shows low MSAFP and estriol but high beta-hCG and inhibin A.
explanation.whyCorrect: Down syndrome (trisomy 21) classically produces a quad screen with decreased MSAFP, decreased estriol, and elevated beta-hCG and inhibin A. The elevated beta-hCG and inhibin A distinguish trisomy 21 from other trisomies.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Uniformly elevated markers are not the recognized trisomy 21 pattern.
whyWrongByChoice.B: An isolated MSAFP elevation with otherwise normal markers suggests an open neural tube defect.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A pattern with all four markers low is characteristic of Edwards syndrome (trisomy 18), not trisomy 21.
whyWrongByChoice.E: An isolated beta-hCG elevation is characteristic of gestational trophoblastic disease, not trisomy 21.

questions.topicName: Prenatal Genetic Testing & Neonatal Screening

questions.stem: A 36-year-old woman underwent prenatal testing at 17 weeks of gestation. Her quad screen results are: AFP 0.72 MoM, uE3 (estriol) 0.80 MoM, hCG 0.75 MoM, and inhibin A 1.08 MoM. These values are most consistent with an increased risk for which of the following conditions?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Neural tube defect

choices.label: B
choices.text: No increased risk

choices.label: C
choices.text: Trisomy 13

choices.label: D
choices.text: Trisomy 18

choices.label: E
choices.text: Trisomy 21

explanation.summary: Low MSAFP, low estriol, low hCG, and normal inhibin A indicate increased risk for trisomy 18.
explanation.whyCorrect: Lower-than-expected MSAFP and estriol are seen in the commonly tested trisomies, but the low hCG together with a normal (not elevated) inhibin A points specifically to trisomy 18 (Edwards syndrome).

whyWrongByChoice.A: A neural tube defect would produce an elevated (high) MSAFP, whereas this MSAFP is low.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Multiple abnormal analyte values indicate an increased risk of some kind, so 'no increased risk' is incorrect.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Second-trimester quad screening is not sensitive or specific for trisomy 13, so it does not give a reliable risk estimate for it.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Trisomy 21 would show elevated hCG and inhibin A, which are not present here.

questions.topicName: Prenatal Genetic Testing & Neonatal Screening

questions.stem: A 28-year-old woman has a quad screen at 16 weeks of gestation that shows a markedly elevated maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein (MSAFP), with an AFP MoM of 3.2. The remaining analytes are within normal limits. This result should most raise concern for which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Klinefelter syndrome (47,XXY)

choices.label: B
choices.text: Open neural tube defect

choices.label: C
choices.text: Trisomy 13 (Patau syndrome)

choices.label: D
choices.text: Trisomy 18 (Edwards syndrome)

choices.label: E
choices.text: Trisomy 21 (Down syndrome)

explanation.summary: High maternal serum AFP raises concern for an open neural tube defect.
explanation.whyCorrect: When a fetus has an open neural tube defect, AFP leaks directly into the amniotic fluid and subsequently reaches the maternal circulation, producing elevated serum levels. About 80% of pregnancies affected by open NTDs have AFP MoM values greater than 2.50.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Sex chromosome aneuploidies are not detected by an isolated MSAFP elevation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Second-trimester screening is not sensitive or specific for trisomy 13, and it is not associated with elevated MSAFP.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Trisomy 18 is associated with low MSAFP.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Trisomy 21 is associated with low, not high, MSAFP.

questions.topicName: Prenatal Genetic Testing & Neonatal Screening

questions.stem: A patient is counseled about noninvasive prenatal testing (NIPT) at 11 weeks of gestation. The clinician explains that the test analyzes cell-free DNA in the mother's blood. The fetal-origin cell-free DNA analyzed by this test enters the maternal circulation primarily through which of the following mechanisms?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Active transport of intact fetal lymphocytes across the placenta

choices.label: B
choices.text: Apoptosis of placental trophoblast cells releasing DNA fragments

choices.label: C
choices.text: Breakdown of maternal white blood cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: Diffusion of amniocytes into the amniotic fluid

choices.label: E
choices.text: Hemolysis of fetal red blood cells in the maternal spleen

explanation.summary: Fetal cell-free DNA reaches maternal blood via apoptosis of placental trophoblasts.
explanation.whyCorrect: The fetal fraction of cell-free DNA gets into the maternal circulation through the placenta when apoptosis occurs in trophoblast cells. After roughly 10 weeks of gestation the fetal fraction is high enough to perform the test, which uses massively parallel (next-generation) sequencing to detect extra or missing chromosomal material.

whyWrongByChoice.A: NIPT analyzes cell-free DNA fragments, not intact fetal cells actively transported across the placenta.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The clinically useful signal is the fetal (placental) DNA fraction, not maternal white cell breakdown.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Amniocytes are cells found in amniotic fluid and are relevant to amniocentesis, not to cell-free DNA in maternal serum.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The test does not depend on hemolysis of fetal red cells.

questions.topicName: Prenatal Genetic Testing & Neonatal Screening

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman presents at 12 weeks of gestation for her first-trimester combined screening. In addition to a nuchal translucency measurement on ultrasound, which of the following pairs of maternal serum markers make up this combined screen?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Estriol and pregnancy-associated plasma protein A in maternal serum

choices.label: B
choices.text: Inhibin A and unconjugated estriol in maternal serum

choices.label: C
choices.text: MSAFP and estriol measured in maternal serum

choices.label: D
choices.text: MSAFP and inhibin A measured in maternal serum

choices.label: E
choices.text: Pregnancy-associated plasma protein A and free beta-hCG

explanation.summary: The first-trimester combined screen is nuchal translucency plus PAPP-A and free beta-hCG.
explanation.whyCorrect: The first-trimester combined screening test uses the nuchal translucency measurement on ultrasound together with two maternal serum biomarkers: pregnancy-associated plasma protein A (PAPP-A) and free beta-hCG.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Estriol is a second-trimester marker; only PAPP-A is a first-trimester marker.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Inhibin A and estriol are second-trimester quad screen markers.
whyWrongByChoice.C: MSAFP and estriol are part of the second-trimester quad screen, not the first-trimester screen.
whyWrongByChoice.D: MSAFP and inhibin A belong to the quad screen.

questions.topicName: Prenatal Genetic Testing & Neonatal Screening

questions.stem: A couple in their late twenties who have been unable to conceive naturally present for a consultation about in vitro fertilization. Both have relatives affected by an inherited genetic disorder and are worried about passing it on. They ask whether embryos can be tested for the specific mutation before a pregnancy is established. Which of the following describes the appropriate test?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amniocentesis in the second trimester

choices.label: B
choices.text: Anatomy ultrasound in the second trimester

choices.label: C
choices.text: Chorionic villus sampling in the first trimester

choices.label: D
choices.text: Noninvasive prenatal testing of cell-free DNA

choices.label: E
choices.text: Preimplantation genetic diagnosis

explanation.summary: Preimplantation genetic diagnosis tests a day-5 embryo during IVF, before implantation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Preimplantation genetic diagnosis (PGD) tests whether a specific genetic change is present in a day-5 embryo (blastocyst) as part of in vitro fertilization. A biopsy removes about 3-8 cells from each blastocyst, and the embryo is usually frozen and implanted later only if unaffected.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Amniocentesis is performed on an already established pregnancy in the second trimester.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Ultrasound provides anatomic imaging, not genetic information, and requires an established pregnancy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: CVS is performed on an already established pregnancy in the first trimester.
whyWrongByChoice.D: NIPT is a maternal blood screening test done during an established pregnancy.

questions.topicName: Prenatal Genetic Testing & Neonatal Screening

questions.stem: A pregnant patient at 20 weeks of gestation has a serum alpha-fetoprotein concentration of 90 ng/mL. The median AFP for unaffected pregnancies at this gestational age in the laboratory's population is 45 ng/mL. What is this patient's AFP expressed as a multiple of the median (MoM)?

explanation.summary: MoM equals the patient's result divided by the population median: 90/45 = 2.0.
explanation.whyCorrect: Multiple of the median (MoM) is calculated as the patient's result divided by the median of the unaffected matched patient population. Here, 90 ng/mL divided by the median of 45 ng/mL equals a MoM of 2.0.

whyWrongByChoice.A: 0.5 would require the patient's value to be half the median.
whyWrongByChoice.B: 1.0 is the expected MoM under normal circumstances (patient value equal to the median).
whyWrongByChoice.D: 3.0 would require a patient value of 135 ng/mL.
whyWrongByChoice.E: 4.0 would require a patient value of 180 ng/mL.

questions.topicName: Prenatal Genetic Testing & Neonatal Screening

questions.stem: A 39-year-old woman undergoes chorionic villus sampling at 11 weeks of gestation. Analysis of the sampled tissue provides fetal genetic information because the cells obtained are derived from which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amniotic fluid surrounding the fetus

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fetal blood drawn from the umbilical cord

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fetal skin cells shed into the amniotic cavity

choices.label: D
choices.text: Maternal decidua of the uterine lining

choices.label: E
choices.text: Trophoblast cells of the placental villi

explanation.summary: CVS samples chorionic villus trophoblast, which is derived from the extraembryonic part of the embryo.
explanation.whyCorrect: CVS involves a biopsy of tissue from the villi of the chorion. The trophoblast cells in the chorionic villi are derived from the extraembryonic part of the early developing embryo and are therefore a source of fetal genetic tissue. The procedure is performed under continuous ultrasound visualization.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Amniotic fluid is sampled during amniocentesis, not CVS.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Umbilical cord blood sampling is a different procedure and is not what CVS collects.
whyWrongByChoice.C: CVS samples chorionic villi, not shed fetal skin cells in the amniotic cavity.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Maternal decidua is maternal tissue and would not provide fetal genetic information.

questions.topicName: Prenatal Genetic Testing & Neonatal Screening

questions.stem: A term newborn is being evaluated in the nursery. As part of routine newborn screening for metabolic disorders, which of the following describes how the sample is obtained and analyzed?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amniotic fluid obtained by amniocentesis and analyzed by next-generation sequencing

choices.label: B
choices.text: Buccal swab collected at the bedside and analyzed by chromosomal microarray

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cord blood collected at delivery and sent for G-banded karyotype analysis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Dried blood collected by heel stick and analyzed by tandem mass spectrometry

choices.label: E
choices.text: Maternal serum analyzed for cell-free fetal DNA in the third trimester

explanation.summary: Newborn metabolic screening uses dried blood from a heel stick, analyzed by tandem mass spectrometry.
explanation.whyCorrect: Metabolic disorder screening tests use a sample of the neonate's dried blood collected by heel stick. Samples are then analyzed by tandem mass spectrometry or disease-specific methods. Metabolic disorders were among the first conditions included because early detection improves outcomes.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Amniotic fluid is obtained prenatally by amniocentesis, not from a newborn.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A buccal swab with microarray is not the standard newborn metabolic screening method.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Routine newborn metabolic screening does not use cord-blood karyotyping.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Cell-free DNA from maternal serum is a prenatal screening test, not a newborn screen.

questions.topicName: Prenatal Genetic Testing & Neonatal Screening

questions.stem: A 35-year-old woman has a noninvasive prenatal test (NIPT) that returns a high-probability (positive) result for trisomy 21. She asks whether this means her fetus definitely has Down syndrome. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step to establish a diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Order a second-trimester quad screen

choices.label: B
choices.text: Perform a diagnostic test such as amniocentesis or CVS

choices.label: C
choices.text: Perform an anatomy ultrasound as the confirmatory test

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reassure the patient that no further testing is needed

choices.label: E
choices.text: Repeat the NIPT at a later date

explanation.summary: A positive screening result must be confirmed with a diagnostic test.
explanation.whyCorrect: All prenatal screening tests, including NIPT, estimate risk as higher or lower but are not diagnostic. A screen indicating increased risk must still be confirmed with a diagnostic test that examines fetal cells directly, such as amniocentesis or chorionic villus sampling with karyotype analysis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The quad screen is another screening test and cannot confirm the diagnosis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ultrasound can raise suspicion but is not diagnostic for a chromosomal abnormality.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A positive screen indicates increased risk and requires confirmatory diagnostic testing, not reassurance alone.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Repeating a screening test does not establish a diagnosis.

questions.topicName: Prenatal Genetic Testing & Neonatal Screening

questions.stem: A 33-year-old woman at 12 weeks of gestation undergoes first-trimester combined screening. The ultrasound shows an increased nuchal translucency, and serum testing reveals a low PAPP-A with an elevated free beta-hCG. This marker profile is most consistent with an increased risk for which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Open neural tube defect

choices.label: B
choices.text: Trisomy 13 (Patau syndrome)

choices.label: C
choices.text: Trisomy 18 (Edwards syndrome)

choices.label: D
choices.text: Trisomy 21 (Down syndrome)

choices.label: E
choices.text: Turner syndrome (45,X)

explanation.summary: In the first trimester, low PAPP-A with high beta-hCG and increased nuchal translucency points to trisomy 21.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the first-trimester combined screen, trisomy 21 shows a low PAPP-A but an elevated beta-hCG, along with an increased nuchal translucency. Down syndrome is the only routinely screened trisomy in which beta-hCG is high rather than low.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Neural tube defects are detected by an elevated second-trimester MSAFP, and the first-trimester screen gives no information on NTDs.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Trisomy 13 shows low PAPP-A and low beta-hCG.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Trisomy 18 shows low PAPP-A and low beta-hCG, not an elevated beta-hCG.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Turner syndrome is a sex chromosome aneuploidy and is not defined by this first-trimester serum trisomy pattern.

questions.topicName: Prenatal Genetic Testing & Neonatal Screening

questions.stem: A 33-year-old woman at 17 weeks of gestation undergoes amniocentesis for fetal karyotype analysis. In addition to the karyotype, the laboratory reports an alpha-fetoprotein level measured directly in the amniotic fluid sample. This additional measurement is most useful for evaluating the risk of which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A 22q11.2 microdeletion

choices.label: B
choices.text: A neural tube defect

choices.label: C
choices.text: An inherited metabolic disorder

choices.label: D
choices.text: Critical congenital heart disease

choices.label: E
choices.text: Trisomy 13

explanation.summary: AFP measured in amniotic fluid obtained at amniocentesis is informative for neural tube defect risk.
explanation.whyCorrect: Alpha-fetoprotein levels can be measured in the amniotic fluid collected during amniocentesis, and this measurement is informative for evaluating the risk of a neural tube defect. AFP from an open defect leaks directly into the amniotic fluid, so the fluid concentration is the most direct reflection of that process.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Microdeletions are identified by chromosomal microarray on the collected cells, not by an AFP measurement.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Metabolic disorders are screened for after birth on the newborn's dried blood spot.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Critical congenital heart disease is screened for after birth using pulse oximetry.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Trisomy 13 is established from the karyotype of the cultured fetal cells, not from the fluid AFP level.

questions.topicName: Prenatal Genetic Testing & Neonatal Screening

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman is counseled about her options for detecting an open neural tube defect in her fetus. Among the prenatal screening modalities, which of the following has the highest detection rate for neural tube defects?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cell-free DNA testing performed at 12 weeks

choices.label: B
choices.text: First-trimester combined screen at 12 weeks

choices.label: C
choices.text: Nuchal translucency measurement at 12 weeks

choices.label: D
choices.text: Second-trimester quad screen at 16 weeks

choices.label: E
choices.text: Targeted anatomy ultrasound at 20 weeks

explanation.summary: Targeted (anatomy) ultrasound detects about 95% of neural tube defects, more than any other screening option.
