explanation.whyCorrect: Ultrasound is more accurate than MSAFP for detection of NTDs; the targeted anatomy ultrasound performed at 18-22 weeks has an NTD detection rate of roughly 95%, compared with about 85% for the quad screen.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cell-free DNA testing provides no information about neural tube defects.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The first-trimester combined screen provides no information about neural tube defects.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Nuchal translucency thickness estimates aneuploidy risk and says nothing about neural tube defects.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The quad screen detects about 85% of NTDs through the MSAFP value, less than ultrasound.

questions.topicName: Prenatal Genetic Testing & Neonatal Screening

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman at 12 weeks of gestation has cell-free DNA testing that reports a low probability for trisomies 21, 18, and 13. Her sister had a child with spina bifida, and she asks whether this result also reassures her about that condition. Which of the following is the most appropriate response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cell-free DNA gives no neural tube defect information; MSAFP or ultrasound is needed.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Chorionic villus sampling is the only way to evaluate neural tube defect risk.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Nuchal translucency measured today will estimate the neural tube defect risk.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Repeating the cell-free DNA test after 15 weeks will detect a neural tube defect.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The low-probability result also makes a neural tube defect unlikely.

explanation.summary: NIPT screens for extra or missing chromosomal material and yields no information on neural tube defects.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cell-free DNA testing looks for evidence of extra or absent chromosomal material and provides no information on NTDs. Evaluation of NTD risk requires second-trimester MSAFP or ultrasound, which is added later in pregnancy.

whyWrongByChoice.B: CVS samples chorionic villi for chromosome analysis and does not evaluate NTD risk.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Nuchal translucency is used for aneuploidy risk, not for neural tube defects.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Repeating cell-free DNA at any gestational age still gives no NTD information.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A low-probability aneuploidy result says nothing about the risk of an NTD.

questions.topicName: Prenatal Genetic Testing & Neonatal Screening

questions.stem: A couple reviewing their cell-free DNA report asks which conditions besides trisomies 21, 18, and 13 are checked. Which of the following is routinely assessed on most cell-free DNA tests?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cri du chat syndrome (terminal 5p deletion)

choices.label: C
choices.text: Prader-Willi syndrome (15q11.2-q13 deletion)

choices.label: D
choices.text: Triploidy

choices.label: E
choices.text: Trisomy 16

explanation.summary: Sex chromosome aneuploidies (45,X; 47,XXX; 47,XXY; 47,XYY) are routinely assessed on most cfDNA tests.
explanation.whyCorrect: Beyond the three common autosomal trisomies that are routinely screened, most cfDNA tests also routinely assess the sex chromosome aneuploidies: 45,X (Turner), 47,XXX (Triple X), 47,XXY (Klinefelter), and 47,XYY (Jacobs).

whyWrongByChoice.B: Cri du chat is a microdeletion syndrome that is detectable but not routinely included.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Prader-Willi syndrome is a microdeletion syndrome not included in routine prenatal screening.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Triploidy is clinically detectable but is not currently recommended for routine prenatal screening.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Rare autosomal aneuploidies such as trisomy 16 are clinically detectable but are not part of routine screening.

questions.topicName: Prenatal Genetic Testing & Neonatal Screening

questions.stem: A pregnant patient whose partner has DiGeorge syndrome (22q11.2 deletion) asks whether the routine cell-free DNA screen being ordered will check the fetus for that deletion. Which of the following statements is most accurate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It becomes detectable by cell-free DNA testing only after 20 weeks of gestation.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It cannot be detected by cell-free DNA testing at any gestational age.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is clinically detectable, but inclusion in routine prenatal screening is not recommended.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is one of the conditions routinely screened by cell-free DNA testing.

choices.label: E
choices.text: It is routinely assessed on most cfDNA tests, as the sex chromosome aneuploidies are.

explanation.summary: Microdeletion syndromes such as 22q11.2 deletion are detectable by cfDNA but are not part of routine prenatal screening.
explanation.whyCorrect: NIPT is clinically available for other aneuploidy and copy-number variant conditions, including microdeletion and microduplication syndromes such as DiGeorge syndrome (22q11.2 deletion), but these are not currently included in routine prenatal screening.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Detection of CNVs does not depend on reaching 20 weeks; cfDNA can be performed after about 10 weeks.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The deletion is clinically detectable by cfDNA; the issue is that it is not routinely included.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Only trisomies 21, 18, and 13 are the routinely screened aneuploidies.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The sex chromosome aneuploidies are routinely assessed, but microdeletions are not.

questions.topicName: Prenatal Genetic Testing & Neonatal Screening

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman at 11 weeks of gestation wants the screening option with the highest detection rate and the lowest false-positive rate for trisomies 21, 18, and 13, and she declines any procedure that carries risk to the pregnancy. Which of the following should be offered?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Anatomy ultrasound at 20 weeks

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cell-free DNA testing (NIPT)

choices.label: C
choices.text: Chorionic villus sampling

choices.label: D
choices.text: First-trimester combined screen

choices.label: E
choices.text: Quad screen at 16 weeks

explanation.summary: NIPT is the most sensitive screening option for the traditionally screened aneuploidies and has the lowest false-positive rate.
explanation.whyCorrect: NIPT is now the most-used screening test for aneuploidies and is currently the most sensitive screening option for trisomies 21, 18, and 13, with detection rates of 90-99% and a false-positive rate lower than other screening options. It is a blood draw, so it carries no procedural risk to the pregnancy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Anatomy ultrasound detects only about 50% of trisomy 21 cases.
whyWrongByChoice.C: CVS is an invasive diagnostic test that carries a slight risk of miscarriage, which she declines.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The first-trimester combined screen detects about 90-98% of the trisomies, still less sensitive than NIPT.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The quad screen detects only about 75-80% of trisomy 21 and 60-80% of trisomy 18.

questions.topicName: Prenatal Genetic Testing & Neonatal Screening

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman establishes prenatal care at exactly 15 weeks of gestation and has had no prior testing. Considering only the recommended timing windows, which of the following tests can be performed at this gestational age?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chorionic villus sampling

choices.label: B
choices.text: First-trimester combined screen

choices.label: C
choices.text: Nuchal translucency ultrasound

choices.label: D
choices.text: Quad screen

choices.label: E
choices.text: Targeted anatomy ultrasound

explanation.summary: The second-trimester quad screen is performed at 15-20 weeks, so its window opens exactly at 15 weeks.
explanation.whyCorrect: The quadruple screen is performed between 15 and 20 weeks of gestation, so a patient presenting at 15 weeks is within that window. The other listed options have windows that have either closed or not yet opened.

whyWrongByChoice.A: CVS is performed at 10-14 weeks, so it can no longer be offered at 15 weeks.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The first-trimester combined screen is performed at 11-14 weeks, so that window has closed.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Nuchal translucency is measured as part of the 11-14 week first-trimester screening ultrasound.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The targeted anatomy ultrasound is performed at 18-22 weeks, which has not yet been reached.

questions.topicName: Prenatal Genetic Testing & Neonatal Screening

questions.stem: A 38-year-old woman at 12 weeks of gestation is scheduled for chorionic villus sampling. Which of the following best describes how the sample is obtained?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Transabdominal needle placement into the amniotic sac

choices.label: B
choices.text: Transabdominal sampling of blood from the umbilical cord

choices.label: C
choices.text: Transcervical brushing of the maternal decidua

choices.label: D
choices.text: Transcervical or transabdominal biopsy of the chorionic villi

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transvaginal aspiration of fluid from the chorionic cavity

explanation.summary: CVS is a biopsy of the villi of the chorion taken transcervically or transabdominally under continuous ultrasound.
explanation.whyCorrect: Chorionic villus sampling involves taking a biopsy of tissue from the villi of the chorion, either transcervically or transabdominally, and the procedure is performed under continuous ultrasound visualization.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Placing a needle transabdominally into the amniotic sac describes amniocentesis, not CVS.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Umbilical cord blood sampling is a different procedure and is not how chorionic villi are obtained.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Maternal decidua is maternal tissue and would not supply fetal genetic material.
whyWrongByChoice.E: CVS obtains villous tissue by biopsy rather than aspirating fluid from the chorionic cavity.

questions.topicName: Prenatal Genetic Testing & Neonatal Screening

questions.stem: A 35-year-old woman is deciding whether to undergo amniocentesis after a high-probability screening result. She asks what could go wrong with the procedure itself. Which of the following should be included in her counseling?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A false-positive trisomy result that requires a repeat screen

choices.label: B
choices.text: A slight risk of miscarriage, bleeding, fluid loss, and infection

choices.label: C
choices.text: An increased risk of a neural tube defect in the fetus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Failure of amniotic fluid cells to yield fetal genetic material

choices.label: E
choices.text: Inability to detect trisomies until the third trimester

explanation.summary: CVS and amniocentesis are invasive and carry a slight risk of miscarriage, bleeding, fluid loss, and infection.
explanation.whyCorrect: Both invasive diagnostic techniques carry increased risks for the fetus and the pregnant person: a slight risk of miscarriage (which varies with location and specialist), as well as bleeding, fluid loss, and infection.

whyWrongByChoice.A: False-positive results belong to screening tests; amniocentesis is a diagnostic test.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Amniocentesis does not cause neural tube defects; amniotic fluid AFP is actually used to assess NTD risk.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Amniotic fluid contains cells of fetal origin that can be cultured for diagnostic testing.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Amniocentesis is performed at 16-20 weeks and is diagnostic for trisomies at that time.

questions.topicName: Prenatal Genetic Testing & Neonatal Screening

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman at 13 weeks of gestation has a family history of spina bifida and wants a definitive answer about both trisomies and a possible neural tube defect. Which of the following single procedures will address both concerns?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amniocentesis at 17 weeks

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cell-free DNA testing now

choices.label: C
choices.text: Chorionic villus sampling now

choices.label: D
choices.text: First-trimester combined screen now

choices.label: E
choices.text: Targeted anatomy ultrasound at 20 weeks

explanation.summary: Amniocentesis is diagnostic for trisomies and detects more than 99% of neural tube defects.
explanation.whyCorrect: Amniocentesis samples amniotic fluid at 16-20 weeks; the cultured fetal cells are diagnostic for trisomies, and the amniotic fluid AFP gives greater than 99% detection of neural tube defects. It is the one listed procedure that addresses both concerns definitively.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Cell-free DNA is a screening test and gives no information about neural tube defects.
whyWrongByChoice.C: CVS is diagnostic for trisomies but provides no evaluation of neural tube defects.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The first-trimester combined screen is not diagnostic and gives no NTD information.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Anatomy ultrasound detects most NTDs but is a screen and detects only about 50% of trisomy 21.

questions.topicName: Prenatal Genetic Testing & Neonatal Screening

questions.stem: Cells obtained by amniocentesis are sent to the laboratory for evaluation of suspected trisomy 21. The collection procedure itself does not establish the diagnosis. Which of the following is used to make the actual genetic diagnosis on the collected cells?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Karyotype or chromosomal microarray

choices.label: B
choices.text: Massively parallel sequencing of maternal cell-free DNA

choices.label: C
choices.text: Measurement of amniotic fluid alpha-fetoprotein

choices.label: D
choices.text: Multiple-of-the-median analysis of serum analytes

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tandem mass spectrometry

explanation.summary: CVS, amniocentesis, and blastocyst biopsy are only means of collecting cells; karyotype or microarray makes the diagnosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: The invasive techniques are the means by which the cells are collected. The actual genetic testing is done by karyotype, chromosomal microarray, gene sequencing, or similar methods, and aneuploidy such as trisomy 21 is identified by karyotype or chromosomal microarray.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Massively parallel sequencing of maternal cell-free DNA is the screening method used for NIPT.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Amniotic fluid AFP informs neural tube defect risk, not chromosome number.
whyWrongByChoice.D: MoM values are how maternal serum screening analytes are reported; they are not run on fetal cells.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tandem mass spectrometry is used on newborn dried blood spots to screen for metabolic disorders.

questions.topicName: Prenatal Genetic Testing & Neonatal Screening

questions.stem: A couple pursuing in vitro fertilization elects preimplantation genetic diagnosis for a familial mutation. Which of the following best describes how the testing and transfer proceed?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cells are biopsied from the blastocyst after it has implanted in the uterine wall

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cells are biopsied from the day-5 blastocyst, which is frozen and transferred later if unaffected

choices.label: C
choices.text: Chorionic villi are sampled once the resulting pregnancy has been established

choices.label: D
choices.text: Maternal serum is analyzed for the familial mutation before the embryo is transferred

choices.label: E
choices.text: The oocyte is tested for the familial mutation before fertilization is performed

explanation.summary: PGD biopsies the day-5 blastocyst; the embryo is usually frozen and implanted later once results confirm it is unaffected.
explanation.whyCorrect: Preimplantation genetic diagnosis tests whether a specific genetic change is present in a day 5 embryo (blastocyst) as part of in vitro fertilization. Cells are removed from each blastocyst and sent to a lab, and the embryo is usually frozen and implanted later, after testing results are confirmed.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The whole point of PGD is that testing occurs before implantation, not after it.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Sampling chorionic villi requires an established pregnancy and is not part of PGD.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Maternal serum analysis is a prenatal screening approach used in an established pregnancy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: PGD is performed on the day-5 embryo after fertilization, not on the unfertilized oocyte.

questions.topicName: Prenatal Genetic Testing & Neonatal Screening

questions.stem: A healthy term newborn undergoes routine newborn screening in the nursery, which includes pulse oximetry testing. This component of the screen is performed to detect which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An open neural tube defect such as spina bifida

choices.label: B
choices.text: Chromosomal aneuploidy such as trisomy 21

choices.label: C
choices.text: Congenital sensorineural hearing loss

choices.label: D
choices.text: Critical congenital heart disease

choices.label: E
choices.text: Inherited metabolic disorders such as phenylketonuria

explanation.summary: Newborn screening includes hearing tests, pulse oximetry for critical congenital heart disease, and metabolic testing.
explanation.whyCorrect: Newborn screening includes hearing tests, pulse oximetry testing to screen for critical congenital heart disease, and testing for metabolic disorders. Pulse oximetry is specifically the component directed at critical congenital heart disease.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Neural tube defects are evaluated prenatally with MSAFP and ultrasound.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Aneuploidy is evaluated prenatally by screening or diagnostic genetic testing, not by pulse oximetry.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hearing loss is screened for with a dedicated hearing test, not with pulse oximetry.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Metabolic disorders are screened using dried blood from a heel stick.

questions.topicName: Prenatal Genetic Testing & Neonatal Screening

questions.stem: Parents who recently moved to a new state notice that their second baby's newborn screening panel lists different conditions than the panel their first baby received. Which of the following best explains this difference?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Only infants with an abnormal physical examination receive the full panel

choices.label: B
choices.text: Screening panels are set nationally and are identical in every state

choices.label: C
choices.text: Tandem mass spectrometry is unavailable in some birth hospitals

choices.label: D
choices.text: The conditions screened depend on the infant's birth weight

choices.label: E
choices.text: The list of metabolic disorders included varies from state to state

explanation.summary: The list of metabolic disorders included in newborn screening varies by state.
explanation.whyCorrect: Newborn screening occurs for almost all children born in a hospital in the U.S., but the specific list of metabolic disorders included in the screen varies by state, which is why panels differ between states.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Newborn screening is performed routinely, not only when the examination is abnormal; in fact conditions are chosen because routine examination will not reveal them.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Panels are not uniform nationally; they are determined state by state.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The samples are analyzed by tandem mass spectrometry or disease-specific methods at the screening laboratory, not at each birth hospital.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Birth weight does not determine which metabolic disorders are screened.

questions.topicName: Prenatal Genetic Testing & Neonatal Screening

questions.stem: Before adopting a new assay, a laboratory demonstrates that the assay measures the concentration of a given analyte accurately and reproducibly. This property of the test is best described by which of the following terms?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Analytical validity

choices.label: B
choices.text: Clinical utility

choices.label: C
choices.text: Clinical validity

choices.label: D
choices.text: Detection rate

choices.label: E
choices.text: Multiple of the median

explanation.summary: Analytical validity is the ability of a test to accurately measure a given analyte.
explanation.whyCorrect: Analytical validity is defined as the ability of a test to accurately measure a given analyte. It is one of three properties providers must consider, alongside clinical validity and clinical utility, when judging whether a test is a good test.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Clinical utility is the ability of the test to affect positive outcomes for the patient.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Clinical validity is the ability of the test to predict the presence of the associated disorder or phenotype.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Detection rate describes the proportion of affected pregnancies a screen identifies, not assay accuracy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Multiple of the median is a way of reporting a screening result relative to a population median.

questions.topicName: Prenatal Genetic Testing & Neonatal Screening

questions.stem: A new assay measures its target analyte accurately and reproducibly, and treatment for the associated condition is available and effective. However, follow-up shows that the analyte level predicts poorly whether a child actually has the associated disorder. Which property of this test is deficient?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Analytical validity

choices.label: B
choices.text: Clinical utility

choices.label: C
choices.text: Clinical validity

choices.label: D
choices.text: Economy of the assay

choices.label: E
choices.text: Turnaround time of the assay

explanation.summary: Clinical validity is the ability of a test to predict the presence of the associated disorder or phenotype.
explanation.whyCorrect: A test can measure its analyte perfectly and still fail to predict whether the person has the associated disorder or phenotype. That predictive ability is clinical validity, and it is what is deficient here.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Analytical validity is intact, since the assay measures the analyte accurately.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Clinical utility concerns whether the test affects positive outcomes; effective treatment is available here.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cost is a practical consideration for screening programs, not the property described.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Speed is a practical requirement for a screening test, not the property described.

questions.topicName: Prenatal Genetic Testing & Neonatal Screening

questions.stem: A state advisory panel considers adding a rare disorder to its newborn screen. A rapid, inexpensive assay detects the disorder with high sensitivity, the disorder is serious and frequent enough to justify screening, it is not apparent on routine newborn examination, and the public health infrastructure can convey and confirm results. However, no therapy changes the course of the disease. Which criterion is not met?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Public health infrastructure can implement follow-up and counseling

choices.label: B
choices.text: Routine observation will not reveal the disorder in the newborn

choices.label: C
choices.text: The assay accurately measures the intended analyte

choices.label: D
choices.text: The condition is frequent and serious enough to justify the expense

choices.label: E
choices.text: Treatment is available and early initiation prevents severe illness

explanation.summary: Clinical utility for newborn screening requires available treatment whose early initiation reduces or prevents severe illness.
explanation.whyCorrect: For clinical utility, a condition must meet criteria that include treatment being available and starting treatment before symptoms manifest reducing or preventing severe illness. Without any therapy that changes the course, this criterion fails even though every other criterion is satisfied.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The scenario states that the infrastructure can convey and confirm results.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The scenario states the disorder is not apparent on routine newborn examination.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The assay is stated to detect the disorder with high sensitivity, so analytical performance is adequate.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The scenario states the disorder is serious and frequent enough to justify screening.

questions.topicName: Prenatal Genetic Testing & Neonatal Screening

questions.stem: A screening program is evaluating candidate laboratory tests for its newborn panel. In addition to being rapid and economical, the chosen test must above all have which of the following characteristics?

choices.label: A
choices.text: High sensitivity, so that affected newborns are not missed

choices.label: B
choices.text: High specificity, so that no healthy newborn is ever retested

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reporting of results as a multiple of the median

choices.label: D
choices.text: The ability to detect the disorder once symptoms have appeared

choices.label: E
choices.text: The ability to run on cord blood rather than heel-stick blood

explanation.summary: A newborn screening test must be rapid, economical, and highly sensitive so there are no false negatives.
explanation.whyCorrect: For a condition to qualify for newborn screening, there must be a rapid and economic laboratory test available that detects what it is intended to detect with high sensitivity, meaning no false negatives. Missing an affected newborn defeats the purpose of screening before symptoms appear.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Screening prioritizes not missing affected infants; screen-positive results are then confirmed.
whyWrongByChoice.C: MoM reporting is used for maternal serum prenatal analytes, not for newborn screening tests.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Screening is specifically intended to detect disorders that routine observation would not reveal, before symptoms manifest.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Metabolic screening uses dried blood collected by heel stick, but the sample type is not the defining requirement.

questions.topicName: Prenatal Genetic Testing & Neonatal Screening

questions.stem: A student asks why maternal serum screening results are reported as multiples of the median rather than being compared with a single fixed reference range. Which of the following is the best explanation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All laboratories share one national median value for these analytes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Analyte levels vary with the stage of pregnancy, so each lab uses its own median

choices.label: C
choices.text: Expressing a result as a ratio converts a screening test into a diagnostic test

choices.label: D
choices.text: The analytes are quantified by massively parallel sequencing rather than immunoassay

choices.label: E
choices.text: Using a median removes the need to establish gestational age by ultrasound

explanation.summary: MoM is used because analyte levels change with gestational stage; each lab divides the result by its own population median.
explanation.whyCorrect: MoM is used when results of individual tests may be highly variable depending on patient profile. In prenatal screening, analyte levels change depending on the stage of pregnancy, so each laboratory must establish its own reference data and median, and the patient's result is divided by the median of the unaffected matched population.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Each laboratory must establish its own reference data and determine the median for its population.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Expressing a result as a MoM does not make a screening test diagnostic; these tests remain screens.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Massively parallel sequencing is used for cell-free DNA analysis, not for serum analyte measurement.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Because analyte levels depend on gestational stage, accurate dating is still required to interpret a MoM.

questions.topicName: Prenatal Genetic Testing & Neonatal Screening

questions.stem: A patient's second-trimester maternal serum AFP is reported as 2.8 MoM. Approximately what proportion of pregnancies affected by an open neural tube defect have an AFP value greater than 2.50 MoM?

explanation.summary: About 80% of pregnancies affected by an open NTD have AFP MoM values greater than 2.50.
explanation.whyCorrect: Approximately 80% of pregnancies affected with open NTDs have AFP MoM values greater than 2.50. This is also why a screen-positive AFP does not infer a definitive diagnosis but indicates that further evaluation should be considered.

whyWrongByChoice.A: 20% would make the cutoff nearly useless as a screen for open NTDs.
whyWrongByChoice.B: 40% understates the performance of MSAFP at this threshold.
whyWrongByChoice.C: 60% understates the proportion above the 2.50 MoM cutoff.
whyWrongByChoice.E: 99% approaches the NTD detection achieved by amniotic fluid AFP at amniocentesis, not by maternal serum AFP.

questions.topicName: Prenatal Genetic Testing & Neonatal Screening

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman undergoes a screening ultrasound at 20 weeks of gestation. Which of the following findings would be considered an ultrasound feature suggestive of aneuploidy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A femur length that is long for gestational age

choices.label: B
choices.text: A low pregnancy-associated plasma protein A level

choices.label: C
choices.text: A nuchal translucency measurement of 1.5 mm at 12 weeks

choices.label: D
choices.text: Elevated alpha-fetoprotein in the amniotic fluid

choices.label: E
choices.text: Pyelectasis of the fetal kidney

explanation.summary: Pyelectasis, choroid plexus cyst, and a short femur or humerus are ultrasound features suggestive of aneuploidy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Additional ultrasound features suggestive of aneuploidy include pyelectasis (a dilated or enlarged renal pelvis), choroid plexus cyst, and the presence of a short femur or humerus. Pyelectasis is the only ultrasound finding among the options.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A short femur or humerus, not a long one, is the feature associated with aneuploidy.
whyWrongByChoice.B: PAPP-A is a first-trimester serum biomarker, not an ultrasound finding.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A nuchal translucency of 1.5 mm is a normal measurement, and an elevated value would be the concerning one.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Amniotic fluid AFP is a laboratory value from amniocentesis and points toward a neural tube defect.

questions.topicName: Prenatal Genetic Testing & Neonatal Screening

questions.stem: A 20-week anatomy ultrasound in a 29-year-old woman demonstrates an abdominal wall defect. This particular finding is most closely associated with which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An open neural tube defect

choices.label: B
choices.text: Down syndrome (trisomy 21)

choices.label: C
choices.text: Klinefelter syndrome (47,XXY)

choices.label: D
choices.text: Patau syndrome (trisomy 13)

choices.label: E
choices.text: Turner syndrome (45,X)

explanation.summary: Abdominal wall defects seen on the anatomy ultrasound are associated with Patau syndrome.
explanation.whyCorrect: The second-trimester screening ultrasound checks for major anatomic abnormalities such as cleft lip, polydactyly, and abdominal wall defects, which are associated with Patau syndrome. Renal anomalies on that same study are associated with both Edwards and Patau syndromes.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Open neural tube defects are detected as spinal or cranial defects on ultrasound and by elevated AFP.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Trisomy 21 is suggested by markers such as increased nuchal translucency and the quad screen pattern, not abdominal wall defects.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Klinefelter syndrome is a sex chromosome aneuploidy assessed on cfDNA and is not linked to this finding.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Turner syndrome is a sex chromosome aneuploidy assessed on cfDNA and is not linked to this finding.

questions.topicName: Prenatal Genetic Testing & Neonatal Screening

questions.stem: A family finally receives a genetic diagnosis for their child after a long diagnostic odyssey. Which of the following is a recognized purpose of establishing a genetic diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It can allow protective care to begin before symptoms appear

choices.label: B
choices.text: It eliminates the need for ongoing clinical follow-up of the child

choices.label: C
choices.text: It establishes the median analyte values used by the laboratory

choices.label: D
choices.text: It guarantees that available treatment will reverse the disorder

choices.label: E
choices.text: It removes the need for newborn screening in future siblings

explanation.summary: A genetic diagnosis can directly change management, including protective care before symptom onset, and informs reproductive risk and family coping.
explanation.whyCorrect: In genetics, a diagnosis can directly impact clinical management, including protective care prior to the onset of symptoms; it can provide reproductive risks for further family planning; and it can provide answers that help families cope with what they are going through and what to expect.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A diagnosis guides management rather than ending clinical follow-up.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Laboratory medians are established from reference populations, not from an individual diagnosis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A diagnosis may improve management, but it does not guarantee that a treatment reverses the disorder.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Newborn screening is still performed for later siblings; a diagnosis informs reproductive risk counseling.

questions.topicName: Prenatal Genetic Testing & Neonatal Screening

questions.stem: A clinician is deciding which laboratory studies fall under the umbrella of clinical genetic testing. Which of the following analyses is considered genetic testing?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Measuring blood pressure at a routine prenatal visit

choices.label: B
choices.text: Measuring nuchal translucency thickness on ultrasound

choices.label: C
choices.text: Measuring oxygen saturation by pulse oximetry in a newborn

choices.label: D
choices.text: Measuring the level of an enzyme that is a gene product

choices.label: E
choices.text: Measuring the volume of amniotic fluid on ultrasound

explanation.summary: Genetic testing includes analysis of chromosomes, DNA, RNA, genes, and gene products such as enzyme levels.
explanation.whyCorrect: Clinical testing related to genetic screening or testing can include the analysis of a wide realm of materials, including human chromosomes, DNA, RNA, genes, and gene products, such as the level of enzymes or other types of proteins. Measuring an enzyme level therefore falls within genetic testing.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Blood pressure is a routine vital sign and involves no genetic material or gene product.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Nuchal translucency is an ultrasound measurement used to estimate aneuploidy risk, not an analysis of genetic material.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Pulse oximetry measures oxygen saturation and is part of newborn screening for heart disease.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Amniotic fluid volume is an ultrasound assessment done before and during amniocentesis.

questions.topicName: Prenatal Genetic Testing & Neonatal Screening

questions.stem: A research team wants to transiently reduce expression of a specific gene in cultured cells for one week without altering the DNA sequence. They introduce a synthetic double-stranded RNA molecule about 21-23 nucleotides long that is loaded into RISC to guide cleavage of the complementary messenger RNA. Which of the following molecules are they using?

choices.label: A
choices.text: miRNA

choices.label: B
choices.text: rRNA

choices.label: C
choices.text: shRNA

choices.label: D
choices.text: siRNA

choices.label: E
choices.text: tRNA

explanation.summary: siRNA is a short double-stranded RNA used for transient gene knockdown.
explanation.whyCorrect: Small interfering RNA (siRNA) is a double-stranded RNA about 21-23 nucleotides long, either synthetic or derived from endogenous dsRNA. Its guide strand is loaded into RISC to direct cleavage of complementary mRNA, producing short-term knockdown without changing the DNA sequence.

whyWrongByChoice.A: miRNA is an endogenously encoded single strand (~22 nt) that broadly regulates gene expression; it is not a synthetic dsRNA introduced for targeted knockdown.
whyWrongByChoice.B: rRNA is a structural and catalytic component of ribosomes and does not silence target genes.
whyWrongByChoice.C: shRNA is a single strand that folds into a hairpin loop and is favored for long-term, stable silencing rather than a brief transient effect.
whyWrongByChoice.E: tRNA delivers amino acids during translation and has no role in RNA interference or gene silencing.

questions.topicName: From Bench to Bedside: The Role of Animal Models in Novel Therapeutics

questions.stem: An investigator needs durable, long-term silencing of a target gene that will persist across many cell divisions. She selects an RNA interference molecule that is a single RNA strand which folds back on itself into a hairpin loop and is processed into siRNA within the cell. Which molecule best fits this description?

choices.label: A
choices.text: miRNA

choices.label: B
choices.text: mRNA

choices.label: C
choices.text: rRNA

choices.label: D
choices.text: shRNA

choices.label: E
choices.text: siRNA

explanation.summary: shRNA folds into a hairpin loop and provides long-term gene silencing.
explanation.whyCorrect: Short hairpin RNA (shRNA) is a single RNA strand that folds into a hairpin loop. It is used for long-term gene silencing in both research and therapeutic applications because it can be stably expressed and processed into siRNA within the cell.

whyWrongByChoice.A: miRNA is an endogenous regulator processed from pri-miRNA to pre-miRNA to mature miRNA; it is not the engineered hairpin construct described.
whyWrongByChoice.B: mRNA carries the coding message for protein synthesis and is the target of silencing, not a silencing tool.
whyWrongByChoice.C: rRNA is a ribosomal component and does not mediate gene silencing.
whyWrongByChoice.E: siRNA is a double-stranded molecule typically used for short-term, transient knockdown rather than durable silencing.

questions.topicName: From Bench to Bedside: The Role of Animal Models in Novel Therapeutics

questions.stem: A student is reviewing the discovery of a natural cellular process in which small RNA molecules silence specific messenger RNAs and defend against viral genomes. This process was first characterized in a small nematode worm, a discovery that earned Andrew Fire and Craig Mello the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 2006. In which model organism was RNA interference originally discovered?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Caenorhabditis elegans

choices.label: B
choices.text: Danio rerio (zebrafish)

choices.label: C
choices.text: Escherichia coli

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mus musculus (mouse)

choices.label: E
choices.text: Saccharomyces cerevisiae

explanation.summary: RNAi was discovered in the nematode C. elegans by Fire and Mello.
explanation.whyCorrect: RNA interference was the first technique used to knock down a gene, and it was discovered in 1998 by Andrew Fire and Craig Mello working in the nematode Caenorhabditis elegans, a discovery recognized with the 2006 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Zebrafish share roughly 70% of genes with humans and are useful vertebrate models, but they are not the organism of the original RNAi discovery.
whyWrongByChoice.C: E. coli is a bacterial non-animal model used to study basic mechanisms but was not where RNAi was discovered.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mice share about 95% of genes with humans and are heavily used, but the seminal RNAi work was performed in C. elegans.
whyWrongByChoice.E: S. cerevisiae (yeast) is a common non-animal model, but the RNAi discovery was made in the worm.

questions.topicName: From Bench to Bedside: The Role of Animal Models in Novel Therapeutics

questions.stem: A biotechnology company is developing an allele-specific siRNA therapy for Huntington disease, in which a CAG triplet-repeat expansion produces toxic huntingtin protein. The design targets the mutant HTT transcript while sparing the wild-type allele, and encouraging results have been seen in mouse models. Which of the following remains the single greatest obstacle to translating this therapy into patients?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Delivering the siRNA across the blood-brain barrier

choices.label: B
choices.text: Inability of siRNA to reduce the amount of protein produced

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lack of any mouse model in which to test the approach

choices.label: D
choices.text: Permanent alteration of the patient's DNA sequence

choices.label: E
choices.text: Requirement to edit the germline to achieve any benefit

explanation.summary: CNS delivery is the major hurdle for siRNA therapies targeting neurologic disease.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick emphasizes that delivering siRNA to hard-to-reach tissues such as the central nervous system remains a significant challenge, contributing to longer development timelines and higher costs. For Huntington disease, crossing the blood-brain barrier is the principal barrier to clinical use.

whyWrongByChoice.B: siRNA works precisely by reducing protein production through mRNA degradation, so this is the intended effect, not an obstacle.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Encouraging results have already been demonstrated in mouse models, so lack of a model is incorrect.
whyWrongByChoice.D: siRNA acts at the mRNA level and does not alter the DNA sequence, so permanent DNA change is not the issue.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This is a somatic, non-heritable knockdown strategy and does not require germline editing.

questions.topicName: From Bench to Bedside: The Role of Animal Models in Novel Therapeutics

questions.stem: A hospital pharmacist reviews Givlaari, a novel RNA-based therapy that silences an overexpressed gene and costs approximately $39,000 per vial, with an expected average annual cost near $442,000 per patient. For which condition is this siRNA therapy indicated?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acute intermittent porphyria

choices.label: B
choices.text: Alzheimer disease with early onset

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cystic fibrosis with the F508del variant

choices.label: D
choices.text: Huntington disease with adult onset

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sickle cell disease with frequent crises

explanation.summary: Givlaari is an siRNA therapy for acute intermittent porphyria.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick identifies Givlaari as a novel siRNA treatment for acute intermittent porphyria, costing about $39,000 a vial with an expected annual average of roughly $442,000 per patient, illustrating how cost can limit development of siRNA therapies.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Alzheimer disease is mentioned as a potential siRNA target (for example APP), but it is not the approved Givlaari indication.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cystic fibrosis is not discussed as the indication for Givlaari in the brick.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Huntington disease is a proposed target for allele-specific siRNA but is not the indication for Givlaari.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sickle cell disease is treated by Casgevy, the first FDA-approved CRISPR-Cas9 therapy, not by Givlaari.

questions.topicName: From Bench to Bedside: The Role of Animal Models in Novel Therapeutics

questions.stem: During preclinical testing, a drug is found to cause severe limb malformations (phocomelia) in human fetuses but produced no such defects when tested in rodents, because of species-specific differences in drug metabolism. This historical example is used to illustrate an important principle of drug development. Which principle does it best demonstrate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Animal models have limitations

choices.label: B
choices.text: Drugs safe in rodents are guaranteed to be safe in humans

choices.label: C
choices.text: Preclinical animal testing is unnecessary before human trials

choices.label: D
choices.text: Rodents and humans share no gene homology

choices.label: E
choices.text: Teratogenicity can never be detected in any animal model

explanation.summary: Thalidomide shows that animal model results do not always predict human outcomes.
explanation.whyCorrect: The thalidomide case is presented to highlight that animal models have limitations: because of species-specific drug metabolism, thalidomide caused birth defects in humans but not in rodents. This underscores the importance of understanding model limitations in drug development.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The thalidomide example directly disproves the idea that rodent safety guarantees human safety.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The FDA mandates preclinical animal studies to assess safety and efficacy; the example does not argue they are unnecessary.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Rodents and humans in fact share extensive gene homology (about 95% of genes in mice), so this statement is false.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The point is that some effects are missed in certain species, not that teratogenicity is undetectable in every model.

questions.topicName: From Bench to Bedside: The Role of Animal Models in Novel Therapeutics

questions.stem: A geneticist generates a mouse in which a specific gene has been permanently inactivated, rendering it non-functional or 'null,' and then compares the animal's phenotype to that of wild-type mice to infer the gene's function. Which type of genetically modified model has been created?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chemical mutagenesis model

choices.label: B
choices.text: Chimeric wild-type model

choices.label: C
choices.text: Knock-in model

choices.label: D
choices.text: Knock-out model

choices.label: E
choices.text: RNA interference model

explanation.summary: A knock-out inactivates a gene ('null') to reveal its function versus wild-type.
explanation.whyCorrect: Knock-out (KO) organisms carry an inactivated gene called 'null' because it is non-functional. Comparing the KO phenotype with wild-type animals helps decipher the gene's function; with CRISPR-Cas9, double and triple knockouts have become easier to generate.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Chemical mutagenesis introduces random mutations across the genome and is not a targeted inactivation of one chosen gene.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Wild-type animals serve as the comparison group and are, by definition, not the genetically inactivated model.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A knock-in model has additional or modified genetic information inserted (such as GFP) rather than an inactivated gene.
whyWrongByChoice.E: RNAi produces transient knock-down at the mRNA level without permanently inactivating the gene in the genome.

questions.topicName: From Bench to Bedside: The Role of Animal Models in Novel Therapeutics

questions.stem: To study a protein's localization in living epithelial cells, a lab engineers an animal whose genome carries an additional inserted sequence coding for green fluorescent protein derived from jellyfish, fused to the endogenous protein. Which category of genetically modified model does this represent?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Forward-genetics mutagenesis model

choices.label: B
choices.text: Knock-in model

choices.label: C
choices.text: Knock-out model

choices.label: D
choices.text: siRNA knock-down model

choices.label: E
choices.text: Wild-type control model

explanation.summary: Inserting new genetic material such as jellyfish GFP defines a knock-in model.
explanation.whyCorrect: Knock-in animals have additional genetic information inserted into their genome. The inserted sequence can be a gene from another species, such as the jellyfish green fluorescent protein (GFP), used here to tag and visualize a protein in living cells.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Forward genetics uses random, untargeted mutagenesis and does not deliberately insert a chosen reporter gene.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A knock-out inactivates a gene rather than adding new genetic material like GFP.
whyWrongByChoice.D: siRNA knock-down reduces expression at the mRNA level and does not add DNA to the genome.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A wild-type control has an unmodified genome and no inserted reporter sequence.

questions.topicName: From Bench to Bedside: The Role of Animal Models in Novel Therapeutics

questions.stem: A researcher exposes a population of worms to a mutagen that introduces random single-nucleotide changes throughout the genome, including coding and non-coding regions, and then screens the offspring for interesting phenotypes such as defects in cell division and apoptosis. This unbiased approach can generate models but cannot be used as a therapeutic strategy. Which method is being described?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Allele-specific siRNA silencing of a transcript

choices.label: B
choices.text: Chemical mutagenesis (forward genetics)

choices.label: C
choices.text: CRISPR-Cas9 targeted genome editing

choices.label: D
choices.text: Homologous recombination at a chosen locus

choices.label: E
choices.text: Targeted knock-in of a fluorescent reporter gene

explanation.summary: Chemical mutagenesis is a random, forward-genetics approach that cannot be therapeutic.
explanation.whyCorrect: Chemical mutagenesis introduces random mutations throughout the genome, and mutants are identified through phenotypic screening. As a forward-genetics (unbiased) technique, it generates models but is not gene-targeted, so it cannot serve as a therapeutic strategy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Allele-specific siRNA silencing is highly sequence-specific and targeted, not random.
whyWrongByChoice.C: CRISPR-Cas9 is a precise, targeted editing tool guided to a specific sequence, the opposite of random mutagenesis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Homologous recombination is a reverse-genetics method that deliberately targets a specific gene, not a random approach.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A targeted knock-in deliberately inserts a chosen sequence at a defined site rather than introducing random mutations.

questions.topicName: From Bench to Bedside: The Role of Animal Models in Novel Therapeutics

questions.stem: A team generates a knock-out mouse using homologous recombination. They electroporate embryonic stem cells with a plasmid carrying a cassette flanked by sequences from the gene of interest, then need a way to identify which cells successfully integrated the cassette before injecting them into blastocysts. What is the primary purpose of including a neomycin-resistance gene in the cassette?

choices.label: A
choices.text: To allow selection of the cells in which the construct was inserted

choices.label: B
choices.text: To degrade the target messenger RNA in the transfected stem cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: To prevent the formation of chimeric offspring after blastocyst injection

choices.label: D
choices.text: To provide the guide RNA that directs the cut site in the genome

choices.label: E
choices.text: To restore function of the disrupted gene of interest in the mouse

explanation.summary: The neomycin-resistance gene is a selection marker for successfully edited cells.
explanation.whyCorrect: In homologous recombination, a cassette containing a neomycin-resistance gene is inserted into the targeted gene, disrupting it. The resistance gene lets researchers select cells that integrated the cassette; these are then injected into blastocysts to produce chimeric mice, which are bred to obtain heterozygous and homozygous animals.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Degrading target mRNA is the function of RNA interference, not a resistance-marker gene.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Chimeric offspring are the intended intermediate step; the marker enables selection and does not prevent chimerism.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Guide RNA is a component of CRISPR-Cas9, not the neomycin cassette used in classic homologous recombination.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The cassette disrupts the gene of interest to knock it out; it does not restore its function.

questions.topicName: From Bench to Bedside: The Role of Animal Models in Novel Therapeutics

questions.stem: In a CRISPR-Cas9 experiment, the Cas9 protein and a guide RNA are delivered into cells and make a precise double-strand break three base pairs upstream of the PAM site. The cell then repairs the break using non-homologous end joining. Which consequence of this repair pathway most directly produces a gene knockout?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Degradation of the gene's messenger RNA by RISC

choices.label: B
choices.text: Exchange of DNA between two homologous chromosomes during meiosis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Insertion of a jellyfish GFP reporter sequence

choices.label: D
choices.text: Introduction of small insertions or deletions causing a frameshift

choices.label: E
choices.text: Precise, error-free restoration of the original sequence

explanation.summary: NHEJ is error-prone and creates indels that cause frameshift knockouts.
explanation.whyCorrect: After Cas9 cuts the DNA about three base pairs upstream of the PAM, the cell attempts repair by non-homologous end joining (NHEJ). NHEJ is error-prone and often introduces small insertions or deletions (indels) that cause frameshift mutations, disrupting the targeted gene and creating a knockout.

whyWrongByChoice.A: mRNA degradation by RISC is the RNA interference mechanism, not the outcome of DNA repair after a Cas9 cut.
whyWrongByChoice.B: DNA exchange between homologous chromosomes describes meiotic recombination, not the NHEJ repair of a Cas9 break.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Inserting a GFP reporter is a knock-in achieved through homologous recombination with a donor template, not through NHEJ indels.
whyWrongByChoice.E: NHEJ is characteristically error-prone; error-free restoration would not disrupt the gene or create a knockout.

questions.topicName: From Bench to Bedside: The Role of Animal Models in Novel Therapeutics

questions.stem: A biotech firm is optimizing guide RNA design and engineering higher-specificity Cas9 variants before advancing a CRISPR-based therapy toward the clinic. Their main worry is that mismatches between the guide RNA and the genome could cause unintended cuts, potentially producing unwanted knockouts or disrupting regulatory regions and raising the risk of tumor formation. Which limitation of CRISPR-Cas9 are they primarily trying to minimize?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ethical concerns over germline editing

choices.label: B
choices.text: High treatment cost

choices.label: C
choices.text: Low editing efficiency

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mosaicism

choices.label: E
choices.text: Off-target effects

explanation.summary: Off-target effects are the biggest technical concern with CRISPR-Cas9.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that the biggest issue with CRISPR-Cas9 is off-target effects, unintended cuts caused by mismatches between the guide RNA and the genome. These can produce unwanted knockouts or disrupt regulatory regions and carry a significant risk of tumor formation, which is why better guide-RNA software and higher-specificity Cas9 proteins have been developed.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ethical concerns, such as those raised by germline editing, are important but are not the technical limitation targeted by improving guide RNA and Cas9 specificity.
whyWrongByChoice.B: High cost limits accessibility (for example, Casgevy exceeding $2 million per patient) but is a separate issue from the unintended-cut problem being addressed.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Low efficiency is a real challenge but is explicitly not identified as the major concern.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mosaicism, the coexistence of edited and non-edited cells, reduces treatment efficacy but is described as a lesser concern than off-target effects.

questions.topicName: From Bench to Bedside: The Role of Animal Models in Novel Therapeutics

questions.stem: A laboratory is selecting a vertebrate model for a study of organ development and compares how closely each candidate species' genome resembles the human genome. The team notes that mice share about 95% of their genes with humans. Approximately what percentage of genes does the other candidate, the zebrafish, share with humans?

explanation.summary: Zebrafish and humans share about 70% of their genes.
explanation.whyCorrect: Using animals as models depends on gene homology, genes with common ancestry. About 95% of genes are shared between mice and humans, and about 70% between zebrafish and humans, which is why many diseases are shared between model organisms and humans with similar genetic causes.

whyWrongByChoice.A: 30% understates the homology; the zebrafish figure given is substantially higher.
whyWrongByChoice.B: 50% is not the figure cited for zebrafish-human gene sharing.
whyWrongByChoice.D: 85% falls between the two quoted values but corresponds to neither species.
whyWrongByChoice.E: 95% is the figure for mice and humans, not for zebrafish.

questions.topicName: From Bench to Bedside: The Role of Animal Models in Novel Therapeutics

questions.stem: An investigator wants to lower the amount of a protein in cultured cells using a reagent that leaves the target transcript intact but blocks the step that converts that messenger RNA into protein. Which of the two main knock-down strategies is she using?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Degradation of the messenger RNA

choices.label: B
choices.text: Excision of the coding region by a nuclease

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inhibition of translation

choices.label: D
choices.text: Insertion of a cassette into the gene

choices.label: E
choices.text: Random mutagenesis of the genome

explanation.summary: Knock-down works either by degrading mRNA or by inhibiting its translation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Knock-down techniques act at the mRNA level with the goal of decreasing the amount of protein produced. Two main strategies are used: mRNA degradation, which breaks down the transcript before it can be translated, and translation inhibition, which blocks the conversion of mRNA into protein while the transcript itself persists.

whyWrongByChoice.A: mRNA degradation destroys the transcript, whereas the stem specifies that the transcript remains intact.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Nuclease excision changes the DNA sequence, which knock-down techniques specifically avoid.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cassette insertion disrupts the gene itself and produces a knock-out, not a knock-down.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Random mutagenesis alters DNA throughout the genome and is not targeted to one transcript.

questions.topicName: From Bench to Bedside: The Role of Animal Models in Novel Therapeutics

questions.stem: Exome sequencing of a family with an undiagnosed developmental disorder identifies six candidate genes. Before committing to one as a therapeutic target, the group selectively reduces the expression of each gene in an animal model and looks for changes in development, behavior, or cellular processes that resemble the patients' findings. What is the principal purpose of these knock-down experiments?

choices.label: A
choices.text: To generate random mutations that can be screened for phenotypes

choices.label: B
choices.text: To insert a fluorescent reporter into each candidate gene

choices.label: C
choices.text: To measure species differences in drug metabolism before trials

choices.label: D
choices.text: To permanently correct the causative mutation in the patients

choices.label: E
choices.text: To validate which candidate gene has a causal role in the disease

explanation.summary: Knock-down models validate the functional relevance of candidate genes found by sequencing.
explanation.whyCorrect: After exome or genome sequencing identifies candidate genes, knock-down models are used to validate their functional relevance. If knock-down animals show phenotypes similar to those of patients, the case that the gene plays a causal role in the disease is strengthened, which guides identification of therapeutic targets.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Random mutation generation is the province of chemical mutagenesis, an unbiased forward-genetics approach.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Inserting a reporter such as GFP creates a knock-in model and is not what reducing expression accomplishes.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Species differences in metabolism are a limitation of animal models, illustrated by thalidomide, not the aim of these experiments.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Knock-down reduces expression transiently and does not alter or correct any DNA sequence in a patient.

questions.topicName: From Bench to Bedside: The Role of Animal Models in Novel Therapeutics

questions.stem: Small RNA molecules made by a cell silence complementary transcripts even when no experimental construct has been introduced. Apart from regulating the cell's own gene expression, what natural function does this pathway serve?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Defending the cell against viral genomes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Delivering amino acids to the ribosome during translation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Exchanging DNA between homologous chromosomes in meiosis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Repairing double-strand breaks in genomic DNA

choices.label: E
choices.text: Selecting cells that have integrated a resistance cassette

explanation.summary: RNA interference is a natural process for gene regulation and antiviral defense.
explanation.whyCorrect: RNA interference is a natural biological process that cells use both to regulate gene expression and to defend against viral genomes. Small RNA molecules silence specific messenger RNAs and reduce their translation into proteins.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Delivering amino acids during translation is the role of transfer RNA, not of the silencing pathway.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Exchange of DNA between homologous chromosomes describes homologous recombination during meiosis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Repair of double-strand breaks is carried out by cellular repair systems such as non-homologous end joining.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Selection of edited cells depends on a neomycin-resistance marker introduced by the experimenter.

questions.topicName: From Bench to Bedside: The Role of Animal Models in Novel Therapeutics

questions.stem: An endogenously encoded single-stranded RNA about 22 nucleotides long acts as a natural regulator of gene expression in a cell. Which sequence correctly describes how this molecule is produced?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Double-stranded siRNA, then hairpin loop, then primary miRNA

choices.label: B
choices.text: Mature miRNA, then precursor miRNA, then primary miRNA

choices.label: C
choices.text: Messenger RNA, then transfer RNA, then mature miRNA

choices.label: D
choices.text: Precursor miRNA, then ribosomal RNA, then mature miRNA

choices.label: E
choices.text: Primary miRNA, then precursor miRNA, then mature miRNA

explanation.summary: miRNA is transcribed as pri-miRNA, processed to pre-miRNA, then to mature miRNA.
explanation.whyCorrect: MicroRNA is a single strand of about 22 nucleotides that is endogenously encoded. It is transcribed as primary miRNA (pri-miRNA), processed into precursor miRNA (pre-miRNA), and then into mature miRNA, which acts as a natural regulator of gene expression.

whyWrongByChoice.A: siRNA is a separate double-stranded species and is not an intermediate in miRNA maturation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This reverses the pathway; the mature form is the end product, not the starting transcript.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Transfer RNA functions in translation and is not a step in producing a mature miRNA.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ribosomal RNA is a structural component of ribosomes and plays no part in miRNA processing.

questions.topicName: From Bench to Bedside: The Role of Animal Models in Novel Therapeutics

questions.stem: Long double-stranded RNA produced endogenously within a cell is cut into duplexes roughly 21-23 nucleotides long that have a guide strand and a non-guide strand; these are then loaded with Argonaute into the silencing complex. Which component performs this initial processing step?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Argonaute (Ago)

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cas9

choices.label: C
choices.text: Dicer

choices.label: D
choices.text: The assembled RISC complex

choices.label: E
choices.text: The tracrRNA scaffold

explanation.summary: Dicer processes endogenous double-stranded RNA into siRNA duplexes.
explanation.whyCorrect: Endogenous double-stranded RNA is processed by Dicer into siRNA of about 21-23 nucleotides, consisting of a guide strand and a non-guide strand. Argonaute and the RISC proteins then assemble on this duplex before the strands are separated.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Argonaute is a component of the silencing complex that assembles on the siRNA after it has already been generated.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cas9 is a bacterial nuclease that cuts DNA at a site specified by a guide RNA, not one that processes cellular dsRNA.
whyWrongByChoice.D: RISC acts downstream, unwinding the duplex and using the guide strand to find and cleave target mRNA.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The tracrRNA-derived scaffold is the constant region of a CRISPR guide RNA and has no role in RNA interference.

questions.topicName: From Bench to Bedside: The Role of Animal Models in Novel Therapeutics

questions.stem: A correctly designed synthetic siRNA is formulated for delivery and is taken into target cells by endocytosis, but it cannot silence its target until one further intracellular event occurs. Which event must take place for the molecule to reach the silencing machinery?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Addition of a PAM sequence to the guide strand

choices.label: B
choices.text: Escape of the siRNA from the endosome

choices.label: C
choices.text: Integration of the siRNA into the genome

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reverse transcription of the siRNA into DNA

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transport of the siRNA into the nucleus

explanation.summary: Endocytosed synthetic siRNA must escape the endosome to reach cytoplasmic RISC.
explanation.whyCorrect: Synthetic siRNA enters the cell by endocytosis and must then undergo endosomal escape into the cytoplasm. Only there can it be loaded with Argonaute and the RISC proteins, unwound, and used to bind and cleave the target mRNA.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A PAM sequence is a feature of CRISPR-Cas9 targeting in DNA and is irrelevant to siRNA function.
whyWrongByChoice.C: siRNA does not alter the DNA sequence, so genomic integration is not part of the mechanism.
whyWrongByChoice.D: siRNA acts directly at the RNA level and is never copied into DNA.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Silencing occurs in the cytoplasm, where RISC binds the exported target mRNA; nuclear entry is not required.

questions.topicName: From Bench to Bedside: The Role of Animal Models in Novel Therapeutics

questions.stem: In a cell treated with siRNA, the loaded silencing complex binds a complementary transcript, cleaves it, and reduced synthesis of the target protein follows. What is the fate of the complex itself once it has cleaved its target?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is converted into a hairpin-loop shRNA

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is degraded together with the cleaved transcript

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is exported to the nucleus to block transcription

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is recycled and can bind additional transcripts

choices.label: E
choices.text: It remains permanently bound to the cleaved fragments

explanation.summary: RISC carrying the guide strand is recycled after cleaving a target mRNA.
explanation.whyCorrect: After unwinding of the siRNA and release of the non-guide strand, the guide strand directs RISC to the target mRNA and cleavage occurs. The complex is then recycled, allowing it to bind further copies of the target transcript, which is why a small amount of siRNA can markedly reduce synthesis of the target protein.

whyWrongByChoice.A: shRNA is a separate engineered hairpin molecule used for long-term silencing, not a product of RISC activity.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Only the target transcript is cleaved; destruction of the complex would end silencing after a single event.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The silencing described acts on cytoplasmic messenger RNA, not on transcription within the nucleus.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Remaining bound to the cleaved fragments would prevent the complex from acting on further transcripts.

questions.topicName: From Bench to Bedside: The Role of Animal Models in Novel Therapeutics

questions.stem: RNA interference has applications well beyond medicine and functional genomics, including a significant role in agriculture. Which agricultural use does it serve?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Editing the germline of livestock to remove disease alleles

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increasing the protein content of harvested grain

choices.label: C
choices.text: Producing pest-resistant and stress-tolerant crops

choices.label: D
choices.text: Replacing chemical fertilizers with engineered viruses

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sterilizing soil bacteria before a field is planted

explanation.summary: In agriculture, RNAi is used to create pest-resistant and stress-tolerant crops.
explanation.whyCorrect: RNA interference is used in agriculture to develop pest-resistant and stress-tolerant crops. By targeting genes in pests or modifying plant responses to environmental stressors, it contributes to more sustainable and resilient farming practices.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Germline editing of animals is a genome-editing application and raises separate ethical concerns.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Raising grain protein content is not among the applications described for RNA interference.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Fertilizer replacement is not an application of RNA interference.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sterilizing soil organisms is unrelated to silencing specific transcripts in pests or plants.

questions.topicName: From Bench to Bedside: The Role of Animal Models in Novel Therapeutics

questions.stem: A team silencing a gene with a single siRNA sequence observes an unexpected new phenotype and suspects that partial homology between their sequence and other transcripts has reduced expression of unintended genes. Which approach best addresses this concern?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Compare treated animals only with untreated wild-type controls

choices.label: B
choices.text: Deliver the same siRNA directly into the central nervous system

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increase the concentration of the original siRNA sequence stepwise

choices.label: D
choices.text: Screen a chemically mutagenized population for that phenotype

choices.label: E
choices.text: Test several different siRNA sequences against the same gene

explanation.summary: Testing multiple siRNA sequences against one gene confirms on-target specificity.
explanation.whyCorrect: Some homology between an siRNA sequence and other messenger RNAs can reduce expression of unintended genes and produce new symptoms. To ensure specificity, multiple siRNA sequences are tested against the same gene; observing a consistent phenotype across different sequences confirms target specificity and argues against an off-target effect.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Untreated controls are already standard and cannot distinguish an on-target from an off-target effect.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Changing the delivery route addresses access to a tissue, not sequence specificity.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Raising the dose of the same sequence would if anything amplify the unintended silencing.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A mutagenesis screen introduces random mutations and does not test whether one siRNA is specific.

questions.topicName: From Bench to Bedside: The Role of Animal Models in Novel Therapeutics

questions.stem: An siRNA therapy is proposed for a neurodegenerative disease characterized by accumulation of beta-amyloid plaques in the brain. Silencing which gene would be the rational target for this approach?

choices.label: A
choices.text: APP

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cas9

choices.label: C
choices.text: CCR5

choices.label: D
choices.text: HTT

choices.label: E
choices.text: krtt1c19e

explanation.summary: APP is the siRNA target proposed for Alzheimer disease because it yields beta-amyloid.
explanation.whyCorrect: siRNA therapies are considered appropriate for Alzheimer disease, including targeting APP, the amyloid precursor protein that produces the beta-amyloid plaques. Reducing the transcript lowers production of the protein that gives rise to the plaques.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Cas9 is a bacterial nuclease used as an editing tool and is not a human disease gene.
whyWrongByChoice.C: CCR5 encodes a surface protein used by HIV to enter immune cells and is unrelated to amyloid plaques.
whyWrongByChoice.D: HTT is the triplet-repeat gene targeted by allele-specific silencing in Huntington disease, not in amyloid plaque disease.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Keratin 19 is used as a fluorescently tagged fusion protein to visualize epithelial cells in research.

questions.topicName: From Bench to Bedside: The Role of Animal Models in Novel Therapeutics

questions.stem: A company weighing investment in an siRNA program notes that such a therapy must be given repeatedly and that one approved siRNA agent averages roughly $442,000 per patient each year. Genome editing technologies are being explored as complementary or alternative strategies. Which feature of genome editing makes it a potentially more favorable cost-benefit strategy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It acts at the messenger RNA level rather than on DNA

choices.label: B
choices.text: It avoids the need to identify the disease-causing gene

choices.label: C
choices.text: It can offer a cure rather than ongoing treatment

choices.label: D
choices.text: It carries no risk of unintended changes to the genome

choices.label: E
choices.text: It crosses the blood-brain barrier more readily than siRNA

explanation.summary: Genome editing may be more cost-effective than siRNA because it can cure rather than treat.
explanation.whyCorrect: The cost of siRNA therapies can limit their development; Givlaari for acute intermittent porphyria costs about $39,000 a vial with an expected annual average near $442,000 per patient. Genome editing is explored as a complementary or alternative strategy because it can offer a cure instead of continuing treatment, potentially a more effective cost-benefit strategy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Acting on mRNA is what siRNA does; genome editing works on DNA, which is precisely why it can be curative.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Editing is a targeted, reverse-genetics approach that requires knowing exactly which sequence to modify.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Off-target cuts are the biggest issue with CRISPR-Cas9 and carry a significant risk of tumor formation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Delivery is if anything harder, since the Cas9 ribonucleoprotein complex is larger and more complex than siRNA.

questions.topicName: From Bench to Bedside: The Role of Animal Models in Novel Therapeutics

questions.stem: Suspecting that excess rather than deficiency of a protein drives a phenotype, an investigator inserts an additional copy of a gene already present in the animal's genome so that it is also expressed in a tissue where it is normally absent. What is this knock-in strategy designed to study?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Loss of gene function in a null animal

choices.label: B
choices.text: Random disruption of unrelated loci

choices.label: C
choices.text: Species differences in drug metabolism

choices.label: D
choices.text: The effect of ectopic or over-expression

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transient reduction of the target transcript

explanation.summary: Adding a second copy of an endogenous gene models ectopic or over-expression.
explanation.whyCorrect: Knock-in animals have additional genetic information inserted into their genome. Besides inserting a gene from another species, another copy of a gene naturally present in the genome can be added in order to study its ectopic or over-expression.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Loss of function in a null animal is what a knock-out produces by inactivating the gene.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Random disruption of unrelated loci characterizes chemical mutagenesis, an untargeted approach.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Species differences in metabolism are a limitation of animal models rather than an aim of this design.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Transient reduction of a transcript is achieved by knock-down methods such as RNA interference.

questions.topicName: From Bench to Bedside: The Role of Animal Models in Novel Therapeutics

questions.stem: Two related genes are thought to compensate for one another, so inactivating either one alone produces no detectable phenotype. Using CRISPR-Cas9, an investigator inactivates both genes in the same animal. What property is this double knock-out designed to reveal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ectopic expression of a reporter gene

choices.label: B
choices.text: Functional redundancy between the two genes

choices.label: C
choices.text: Off-target cutting at mismatched genomic sites

choices.label: D
choices.text: The species-specific metabolism of a drug

choices.label: E
choices.text: The transient effect of silencing a transcript

explanation.summary: Double and triple knock-outs are generated to study genetic redundancy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Double knock-outs, with two genes inactivated in the same animal, can be generated, and with the rise of CRISPR-Cas9 even triple knock-outs have become easier to produce. These multiple knock-outs are particularly useful in research to study redundancy, and the same principle can be applied to multi-loci diseases.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Expression of a reporter requires inserting new genetic material, which defines a knock-in rather than a knock-out.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Off-target cutting is an unwanted side effect of the editing tool, not the biological property under study.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Species-specific drug metabolism is a limitation of animal models, illustrated by thalidomide.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Transient silencing is a feature of knock-down techniques, whereas a knock-out permanently inactivates the gene.

questions.topicName: From Bench to Bedside: The Role of Animal Models in Novel Therapeutics

questions.stem: In a worm mutagenesis screen, an animal with a striking cell-division defect is isolated, but identifying the single nucleotide change responsible was historically laborious because the mutations are random and subtle. Which technical advance most improved the ability to pinpoint the causal mutation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Electroporation of embryonic stem cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fluorescent tagging of proteins with GFP

choices.label: C
choices.text: Neomycin-resistance selection cassettes

choices.label: D
choices.text: Next-generation sequencing

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reagents that promote endosomal escape

explanation.summary: NGS made it feasible to find the causal mutation after a forward-genetics screen.
explanation.whyCorrect: Chemical mutagenesis introduces random mutations throughout the genome, and mutants are recovered by phenotypic screening. Once a mutant is selected, pinpointing the genetic cause is challenging because of the randomness and subtlety of single nucleotide changes, especially before the advent of next-generation sequencing techniques.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Electroporation introduces a targeting plasmid into embryonic stem cells and does not identify unknown mutations.
whyWrongByChoice.B: GFP tagging allows a protein to be visualized but does not locate a random point mutation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A resistance cassette selects cells that have integrated a construct in targeted editing, not in a random screen.
