explanation.summary: The ADRB2 R16G variant increases the risk of asthma exacerbation with long-acting beta-agonists.
explanation.whyCorrect: ADRB2 encodes the beta-2 adrenergic receptor, the target of beta-agonist bronchodilators. The rs1042713 (R16G) variant is listed among GPCR variants that affect drug efficacy and safety, and with LABA ligands it is associated with an increased risk of asthma exacerbation.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Blistering skin reactions reflect HLA-associated immune hypersensitivity, not a receptor variant affecting bronchodilator response.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Memory loss is linked to an HTR2A variant with escitalopram, not to ADRB2 and a beta-agonist.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Myelosuppression follows TPMT deficiency with thiopurine drugs and is unrelated to beta-2 receptor variation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Weight gain is associated with the DRD2 variant and antipsychotic therapy, not with a beta-2 receptor variant.

questions.topicName: Pharmacogenetics: An Introduction

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man with hypertension is started on clonidine. His pharmacogenetic panel reports the ADRA2C deletion variant rs11269124 (Del 322-325). Which of the following effects on clonidine therapy is most likely in this patient?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Decreased ligand binding at the receptor

choices.label: B
choices.text: Decreased receptor expression at the cell surface

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increased efficacy of the drug

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased risk of adverse cardiovascular events

choices.label: E
choices.text: Increased risk of bronchospasm

explanation.summary: The ADRA2C Del 322-325 variant increases clonidine efficacy.
explanation.whyCorrect: ADRA2C encodes an alpha-2C adrenergic receptor, a GPCR drug target. The rs11269124 Del 322-325 variant paired with the ligand clonidine is listed as increasing efficacy, so a greater-than-expected drug effect should be anticipated.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Decreased ligand binding is the effect reported for the ADRB2 T164I variant with salbutamol, not for this ADRA2C deletion.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Decreased receptor expression is described for the OPRM1 N40D variant, not for the ADRA2C deletion.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Increased adverse cardiovascular events are reported for the ADRB1 S49G variant with atenolol and for an HTR2A variant with risperidone.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Bronchospasm risk relates to beta-2 receptor variants and beta-agonist therapy rather than to this alpha-2C deletion.

questions.topicName: Pharmacogenetics: An Introduction

questions.stem: A 34-year-old man with opioid use disorder is transitioned to buprenorphine but reports a poor response at standard doses. Genotyping identifies the OPRM1 variant rs1799971 (N40D). Which of the following best explains the combination of findings expected with this variant?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Decreased beta-endorphin binding affinity with increased receptor expression

choices.label: B
choices.text: Decreased binding affinity with unchanged receptor expression

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increased beta-endorphin binding affinity with decreased receptor expression

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased receptor expression with increased buprenorphine efficacy

choices.label: E
choices.text: Unchanged binding affinity with increased buprenorphine efficacy

explanation.summary: The OPRM1 N40D variant raises beta-endorphin binding affinity while lowering receptor expression and buprenorphine efficacy.
explanation.whyCorrect: OPRM1 encodes the opioid receptor targeted by endogenous opioids and by buprenorphine. The rs1799971 (N40D) variant is reported to increase beta-endorphin binding affinity, decrease receptor expression, and decrease efficacy for buprenorphine, which fits this patient's poor therapeutic response.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The direction of both changes is reversed: binding affinity for beta-endorphin rises and expression falls.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Binding affinity for beta-endorphin increases, and receptor expression does change with this variant.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Expression decreases rather than increases, and buprenorphine efficacy is reduced rather than enhanced.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Binding affinity is not unchanged, and efficacy for buprenorphine falls rather than rises.

questions.topicName: Pharmacogenetics: An Introduction

questions.stem: A 42-year-old man with schizophrenia is maintained on an antipsychotic. His genotype report includes the DRD2 variant rs1799732 (DRD2 PROM -141C Ins/Del). In addition to a reduced response to the medication, which of the following adverse outcomes is he at increased risk for?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Asthma exacerbation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bone marrow suppression

choices.label: C
choices.text: Memory loss

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mucosal blistering

choices.label: E
choices.text: Weight gain

explanation.summary: The DRD2 rs1799732 variant is associated with reduced antipsychotic efficacy and increased weight gain.
explanation.whyCorrect: DRD2 encodes the dopamine D2 receptor, the GPCR target of antipsychotic drugs. The rs1799732 promoter insertion/deletion variant is listed with antipsychotic ligands as decreasing efficacy and increasing weight gain, so weight should be followed in this patient.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Asthma exacerbation is associated with the ADRB2 R16G variant and long-acting beta-agonists.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Bone marrow suppression follows reduced TPMT activity with thiopurine drugs, not a dopamine receptor variant.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Memory loss is the effect linked to the HTR2A rs6311 variant with escitalopram.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mucosal blistering reflects an HLA-associated severe cutaneous reaction rather than a D2 receptor variant.

questions.topicName: Pharmacogenetics: An Introduction

questions.stem: A 58-year-old woman is started on escitalopram for depression. Her pharmacogenetic panel reports the HTR2A variant rs6311. Which of the following is most likely to increase in this patient on escitalopram?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adverse cardiovascular events

choices.label: B
choices.text: Memory loss

choices.label: C
choices.text: Rate of remission

choices.label: D
choices.text: Risk of asthma exacerbation

choices.label: E
choices.text: Weight gain

explanation.summary: The HTR2A rs6311 variant is associated with increased memory loss on escitalopram.
explanation.whyCorrect: HTR2A encodes a serotonin receptor targeted by several psychotropic drugs, and different HTR2A variants pair with different ligands and outcomes. The rs6311 variant with escitalopram is listed as increasing memory loss.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Increased adverse cardiovascular events are reported for the HTR2A rs6313 variant with risperidone, a different variant and ligand.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Improved treatment outcome and remission are reported for the HTR2A rs7997012 variant with antidepressants, not for rs6311.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Asthma exacerbation risk is an ADRB2 effect with beta-agonists and is unrelated to a serotonin receptor variant.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Increased weight gain is the effect attributed to the DRD2 variant with antipsychotics.

questions.topicName: Pharmacogenetics: An Introduction

questions.stem: A 3-year-old boy has polyuria and dilute urine that does not concentrate after administration of desmopressin, and nephrogenic diabetes insipidus is diagnosed. A variant in a G protein-coupled receptor is identified. Which of the following receptors is most likely affected?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Arginine vasopressin receptor 2

choices.label: B
choices.text: Beta-1 adrenergic receptor (ADRB1)

choices.label: C
choices.text: Calcium-sensing receptor (CASR)

choices.label: D
choices.text: Dopamine D2 receptor (DRD2)

choices.label: E
choices.text: Rhodopsin receptor of the retina

explanation.summary: GPCR variants cause specific diseases, and nephrogenic diabetes insipidus maps to arginine vasopressin receptor 2.
explanation.whyCorrect: GPCR mutations have been linked with specific disease occurrences, and arginine vasopressin receptor 2 variants are associated with nephrogenic diabetes insipidus. Failure to concentrate urine despite vasopressin analogue administration points to the renal receptor rather than to a deficiency of the hormone.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Beta-1 adrenergic receptor variants alter antihypertensive response to beta-blockers rather than urine concentration.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Calcium-sensing receptor variants are linked with hypercalcemic syndromes.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Dopamine D2 receptor variants influence antipsychotic efficacy and weight gain.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A mutated rhodopsin receptor is linked with retinitis pigmentosa, a retinal rather than renal disorder.

questions.topicName: Pharmacogenetics: An Introduction

questions.stem: An agonist-bound G protein-coupled receptor is phosphorylated by G protein-coupled receptor kinase, binds arrestin, and is internalized through clathrin and AP-2. After endosomal sorting, which of the following events allows the receptor to be returned to the plasma membrane in a responsive state?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Additional phosphorylation by G protein-coupled receptor kinase

choices.label: B
choices.text: Binding of a second arrestin molecule

choices.label: C
choices.text: Dephosphorylation of the receptor by PP2A

choices.label: D
choices.text: Exchange of GDP for GTP on the G alpha subunit

choices.label: E
choices.text: Recruitment of clathrin and AP-2 to the receptor

explanation.summary: Resensitization of an internalized GPCR requires dephosphorylation by PP2A before recycling.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the GPCR cycle, agonist binding leads to activation and signaling, then GRK phosphorylation and arrestin binding produce desensitization and internalization. After endosomal sorting, PP2A dephosphorylates the receptor, which permits resensitization and recycling back to the plasma membrane.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Further GRK phosphorylation drives desensitization, the opposite of restoring responsiveness.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Arrestin binding to the phosphorylated receptor promotes desensitization and internalization rather than recycling.
whyWrongByChoice.D: GDP-to-GTP exchange on G alpha occurs during activation and signaling at the membrane, not during endosomal recycling.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Clathrin and AP-2 recruitment carries the receptor inward during internalization and does not return it to the surface.

questions.topicName: Pharmacogenetics: An Introduction

questions.stem: A pharmacology review contrasts the two broad classes of drug-metabolizing enzymes. Which of the following best describes the reactions carried out by phase 1 enzymes such as CYP2D6, CYP2C19, and CYP3A4?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Attachment of a large water-soluble molecule that raises molecular weight

choices.label: B
choices.text: Binding of the drug to plasma transport proteins during distribution

choices.label: C
choices.text: Introduction of reactive or polar groups by oxidation, reduction, and hydrolysis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Movement of the drug across the cell membrane by transporter proteins

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transfer of a phosphate group onto the drug by kinases in the hepatocyte

explanation.summary: Phase 1 enzymes add reactive or polar groups to xenobiotics by oxidation, reduction, and hydrolysis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Phase 1 enzymes play a crucial role in drug metabolism by introducing reactive or polar groups into xenobiotics, primarily through oxidation, reduction, and hydrolysis reactions. The most studied phase 1 enzymes in pharmacogenetics are CYP2D6, CYP2C19, and CYP3A4.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Attaching a larger water-soluble molecule describes phase 2 conjugation, carried out by enzymes such as TPMT.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Plasma protein binding relates to drug distribution rather than to phase 1 enzymatic modification.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Membrane movement of drug is the function of drug transporters, not of metabolizing enzymes.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Phosphate transfer is not among the oxidation, reduction, and hydrolysis reactions that define phase 1 metabolism.

questions.topicName: Pharmacogenetics: An Introduction

questions.stem: A student is asked why phase 2 metabolic reactions are described as detoxification pathways. Which of the following best explains the effect of a phase 2 reaction on a drug compound?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It cleaves the compound into reactive fragments for renal filtration

choices.label: B
choices.text: It increases water solubility and molecular weight, easing excretion

choices.label: C
choices.text: It oxidizes the compound so it can bind its receptor more tightly

choices.label: D
choices.text: It reduces molecular weight so the compound crosses membranes faster

choices.label: E
choices.text: It transfers the compound to an immune cell for presentation

explanation.summary: Phase 2 conjugation makes a drug more water soluble and heavier, so the body can excrete it.
explanation.whyCorrect: Phase 2 enzymes attach a larger, water-soluble molecule to the modified compound from phase 1 or sometimes directly to the original compound. This attachment increases the compound's water solubility and molecular weight, making it easier for the body to excrete, which is why these reactions are considered detoxification pathways.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Phase 2 reactions conjugate rather than fragment the compound, and reactive fragments would not be detoxifying.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Oxidation belongs to phase 1 metabolism, and phase 2 conjugation does not enhance receptor binding.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Phase 2 conjugation increases molecular weight rather than reducing it.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Immune presentation underlies HLA-associated hypersensitivity reactions and is not a metabolic conjugation step.

questions.topicName: Pharmacogenetics: An Introduction

questions.stem: A patient carries a variant that causes unusually rapid breakdown of a prescribed medication, so that drug is cleared before it can take effect. Which of the following prescribing adjustments does this metabolizer pattern most likely require?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Less drug than the usual dose

choices.label: B
choices.text: More drug, or a different drug

choices.label: C
choices.text: The usual dose given less frequently

choices.label: D
choices.text: The usual dose given with an immune-suppressing agent

choices.label: E
choices.text: The usual dose with routine marrow monitoring

explanation.summary: Fast breakdown of a drug calls for more drug or a different drug; slow breakdown calls for less.
explanation.whyCorrect: Genetic variants modify the rate at which a drug is metabolized, so one individual needs more drug and another less to achieve the same effect. With fast breakdown the drug is removed before taking effect, so the patient needs more drug or a different drug, whereas normal breakdown needs the usual dose and slow breakdown needs less.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Less drug is the adjustment for slow breakdown, in which the drug builds up and causes side effects.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Spacing the usual dose further apart would lower exposure further in a patient who already clears the drug too quickly.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Adding an immune-suppressing agent addresses neither rapid clearance nor the loss of drug effect it produces.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Marrow monitoring addresses thiopurine toxicity from reduced TPMT activity, which is a slow-breakdown problem.

questions.topicName: Pharmacogenetics: An Introduction

questions.stem: Thiopurine S-methyltransferase (TPMT) methylates thiopurine compounds, and S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine is produced as a byproduct of this reaction. Which of the following serves as the S-methyl donor for this reaction?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 6-mercaptopurine

choices.label: B
choices.text: Azathioprine

choices.label: C
choices.text: S-adenosyl-L-methionine

choices.label: D
choices.text: The heme iron of cytochrome P450

choices.label: E
choices.text: Thiopurine S-methyltransferase itself

explanation.summary: TPMT methylates thiopurines using S-adenosyl-L-methionine as the S-methyl donor.
explanation.whyCorrect: TPMT is a phase 2 enzyme in humans that methylates thiopurine compounds, including thiopurine drugs, via S-adenosyl-L-methionine as the S-methyl donor, with S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine produced as a byproduct. Thiopurine drugs handled this way include chemotherapeutic and immunosuppressive agents.

whyWrongByChoice.A: 6-mercaptopurine is the thiopurine substrate that is methylated and inactivated, not the methyl donor.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Azathioprine is another thiopurine drug substrate whose metabolism depends on TPMT activity.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cytochrome P450 heme iron supports phase 1 oxidation reactions, not phase 2 methyl transfer.
whyWrongByChoice.E: TPMT is the enzyme catalyzing the transfer; it does not supply the methyl group itself.

questions.topicName: Pharmacogenetics: An Introduction

questions.stem: A hematology-oncology clinic is considering pretreatment genotyping before prescribing thiopurine drugs. Approximately what fraction of individuals is deficient for the TPMT enzyme?

choices.label: B
choices.text: 1 in 3

choices.label: C
choices.text: 1 in 30

explanation.summary: About 1 in 300 individuals is deficient for the TPMT enzyme.
explanation.whyCorrect: Genetic polymorphisms affecting TPMT activity correlate with variations in sensitivity and toxicity to thiopurine drugs, and about 1 of 300 individuals is deficient for the TPMT enzyme. Deficiency leads to decreased methylation and inactivation of 6-mercaptopurine and to enhanced bone marrow toxicity.

whyWrongByChoice.A: One in one hundred is higher than the stated frequency of TPMT enzyme deficiency.
whyWrongByChoice.B: One in three would make TPMT deficiency a majority-scale finding rather than the uncommon deficiency described.
whyWrongByChoice.C: One in thirty overstates the frequency of TPMT deficiency by roughly tenfold.
whyWrongByChoice.E: One in three thousand understates the frequency by roughly tenfold.

questions.topicName: Pharmacogenetics: An Introduction

questions.stem: A patient taking a standard dose of a medication has a poor therapeutic response, and the cause is traced to a polymorphism in the gene encoding the protein that carries the drug across the cell membrane. Which of the following best explains the reduced effect?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Less drug is taken up into the cell, lowering drug efficacy

choices.label: B
choices.text: The drug binds its receptor but cannot dissociate from it

choices.label: C
choices.text: The drug is inactivated by methylation before reaching the cell

choices.label: D
choices.text: The drug is oxidized to a reactive metabolite in plasma

choices.label: E
choices.text: The drug is presented to immune cells and destroyed

explanation.summary: Transporter gene polymorphisms alter how much drug enters the cell and therefore how well it works.
explanation.whyCorrect: Drug transporters are proteins that move drugs and other substances across cellular membranes, and polymorphisms in transporter genes significantly impact drug absorption, distribution, and excretion. The efficiency of the transporter alters the amount of drug the cell can take up, which in turn alters the efficacy of the drug.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The problem described lies in delivery of drug into the cell, not in the kinetics of receptor dissociation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Methylation-based inactivation is a phase 2 enzymatic effect, as with TPMT and thiopurines, not a transporter effect.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Oxidation to a metabolite is a phase 1 metabolic step performed by enzymes rather than transporters.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Immune presentation and destruction describe HLA-associated hypersensitivity rather than altered transport.

questions.topicName: Pharmacogenetics: An Introduction

questions.stem: A clinician explains that pharmacogenomic testing is especially valuable for one particular category of medication, exemplified by immunosuppressants used after transplantation. Which of the following defines a drug with a narrow therapeutic index?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The difference between an effective dose and a toxic dose is quite small

choices.label: B
choices.text: The drug acts at a receptor expressed in many different tissues

choices.label: C
choices.text: The drug is metabolized by more than one cytochrome P450 enzyme

choices.label: D
choices.text: The drug must be given with a second agent to be effective

choices.label: E
choices.text: The drug requires a loading dose before maintenance dosing

explanation.summary: A narrow therapeutic index means the effective and toxic doses are close together.
explanation.whyCorrect: Identifying genetic variants known to influence drug metabolism and response helps avoid adverse drug reactions, and this is particularly important for drugs with a narrow therapeutic index, where the difference between an effective dose and a toxic dose is quite small. Small genotype-driven shifts in clearance can therefore push such a drug into the toxic range.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Broad tissue distribution of a receptor may broaden side effects but is not the definition of therapeutic index.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Having several metabolizing enzymes describes a metabolic pathway, not the margin between effect and toxicity.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Requiring combination therapy describes a treatment regimen rather than the dose-toxicity margin.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Requiring a loading dose is a dosing strategy and does not define the therapeutic index.

questions.topicName: Pharmacogenetics: An Introduction

questions.stem: A genetics educator notes that the word used for a change in DNA sequence carries an unintended negative connotation, implying that every such change is harmful or disease-causing. Which of the following changes in terminology did the American College of Genetics and Genomics make to address this?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The term allele was retired and replaced with polymorphism

choices.label: B
choices.text: The term mutation was retired and replaced with variant

choices.label: C
choices.text: The term pathogenic was retired and replaced with benign

choices.label: D
choices.text: The term polymorphism was retired and replaced with genotype

choices.label: E
choices.text: The term variant was retired and replaced with mutation

explanation.summary: The term mutation was replaced by the neutral term variant, with modifiers describing impact.
explanation.whyCorrect: A gene mutation simply means a change in the DNA sequence and does not imply the change is damaging, advantageous, or neutral, yet the word carries a negative connotation. The American College of Genetics and Genomics therefore retired mutation in favor of the more impartial noun variant, then added modifiers to describe how the change may or may not impact gene function.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Allele remains in use for a form of a gene and was not retired in favor of polymorphism.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Pathogenic and benign are both retained as modifiers within the variant classification system.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Polymorphism continues to describe two or more variant forms of a DNA sequence in a population.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The replacement runs in the opposite direction: variant is the newer, neutral term.

questions.topicName: Pharmacogenetics: An Introduction

questions.stem: A researcher studying the genetic features that influence drug response catalogs changes in gene methylation across a patient cohort. Which of the following categories of genetic feature is being studied?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Epigenetic variant

choices.label: B
choices.text: Germline sequence variant

choices.label: C
choices.text: Noncoding RNA change such as an altered microRNA

choices.label: D
choices.text: Somatic mutation acquired in a tumor

choices.label: E
choices.text: Structural chromosomal change such as a translocation

explanation.summary: Changes in gene methylation are epigenetic variants.
explanation.whyCorrect: Besides sequence variants inherited through the germline or acquired, other genetic features studied include structural changes in chromosomes such as translocations, epigenetic variants such as changes in gene methylation, and variation in gene expression profiles including mRNA and noncoding RNA. Methylation changes fall specifically in the epigenetic category.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A germline sequence variant is an inherited change in the DNA sequence itself rather than a methylation mark.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Altered microRNA is a noncoding RNA change within the expression-profile category, not a methylation change.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A somatic mutation, such as one acquired in a tumor, is also a change in DNA sequence.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Translocations are structural chromosomal rearrangements, a separate category from methylation changes.

questions.topicName: Pharmacogenetics: An Introduction

questions.stem: A clinical laboratory director explains that uncovering large numbers of new genetic variants, and building gene panels that can be used for either diagnostic or predisposition testing, has only recently become feasible. Which of the following advances made this possible?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Candidate gene association studies

choices.label: B
choices.text: Genome-wide association studies

choices.label: C
choices.text: Next-generation sequencing

choices.label: D
choices.text: Proteomic profiling of tumor tissue

choices.label: E
choices.text: Therapeutic drug level monitoring

explanation.summary: Next-generation sequencing enables large-scale variant discovery and gene panel testing.
explanation.whyCorrect: Uncovering genetic variants has become feasible thanks to next-generation sequencing, and large-scale sequencing allows generation of gene panels that can be used both for diagnostic and for predisposition testing while uncovering more and more variants. Clinical testing labs then interpret and classify those variants as pathogenic or benign.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Candidate gene association studies test preselected genes for association with drug response rather than generating broad sequencing panels.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Genome-wide association studies look for associations across the genome but are not the sequencing technology that builds diagnostic gene panels.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Proteomic profiling describes protein composition rather than uncovering DNA sequence variants.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Therapeutic drug monitoring measures drug concentrations in a patient and detects no genetic variants.

questions.topicName: Pharmacogenetics: An Introduction

questions.stem: A 61-year-old man with recurrent gout attacks is being considered for urate-lowering therapy, and his physician wants to screen for an HLA allele first because the planned drug is one of those linked to severe HLA-associated reactions. Which of the following drugs is he most likely being prescribed?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Allopurinol

choices.label: B
choices.text: Azathioprine

choices.label: C
choices.text: Metoprolol

choices.label: D
choices.text: Omeprazole

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tacrolimus

explanation.summary: Allopurinol is one of the drugs whose severe reactions are associated with HLA polymorphisms.
explanation.whyCorrect: HLA polymorphisms have been associated with severe reactions to abacavir, allopurinol, and carbamazepine, and these idiosyncratic adverse drug reactions include delayed hypersensitivities such as Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis. Allopurinol is the urate-lowering agent in that group, so HLA screening is relevant before starting it.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Azathioprine toxicity is driven by reduced TPMT activity and myelosuppression, not by HLA-mediated hypersensitivity.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Metoprolol response is influenced by the ADRB1 receptor variant, not by an HLA-associated hypersensitivity risk.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Proton pump inhibitor response is altered by increased-function CYP2C19 variants rather than HLA alleles.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tacrolimus is affected by decreased-function CYP3A4 variants that raise drug levels and cause toxicity.

questions.topicName: Pharmacogenetics: An Introduction

questions.stem: A variant is identified inside a gene but outside its coding region. The amino acid sequence of the encoded protein is unchanged, yet the amount of protein produced is altered and the variant correlates with response to treatment. Which of the following best classifies this variant?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Coding SNP

choices.label: B
choices.text: Copy number variation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Linked (indicative) SNP

choices.label: D
choices.text: Noncoding SNP

choices.label: E
choices.text: Nonsense mutation

explanation.summary: A SNP inside the gene that changes the amount of protein produced is a noncoding SNP.
explanation.whyCorrect: Causative SNPs lie inside the gene and may correlate with disease or response to treatment, and they are subdivided by where they fall. A coding SNP changes the amino acid sequence, whereas a noncoding SNP changes the amount of protein produced, which matches a variant that leaves the protein sequence intact but alters its quantity.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A coding SNP lies in the coding region and alters the amino acid sequence, which did not happen here.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A copy number variation is a deletion or duplication of a DNA segment rather than a single-nucleotide change.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A linked or indicative SNP lies outside the gene and has no effect on protein production or function.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A nonsense mutation truncates the protein as a loss-of-function change in the coding sequence.

questions.topicName: Pharmacogenetics: An Introduction

questions.stem: Two patients of the same age and body size receive identical doses of the same drug, yet one has a much greater response than the other. Approximately what proportion of the differences in drug metabolism and response between patients is attributed to genetic factors?

explanation.summary: Genetic factors account for an estimated 20-40% of interpatient differences in drug metabolism and response.
explanation.whyCorrect: It is estimated that genetic factors are responsible for 20-40% of the differences in drug metabolism and response between patients. Identifying those factors is the goal of pharmacogenomics, which aims to design treatments with improved efficacy and reduced adverse reactions.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A few percent would make genotype a trivial contributor and understates the estimated share.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Half to sixty percent exceeds the estimated genetic contribution to variable drug response.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Seventy to eighty percent would leave little room for the nongenetic factors such as age, sex, and body weight that also contribute.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Nearly all variability being genetic contradicts the role of organ function, age, and body size in drug response.

questions.topicName: Pharmacogenetics: An Introduction

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man with obesity is being dosed for a new medication, and his physician notes that his dosing requirements may differ from those of a patient with lower body weight even though their genotypes are the same. Which of the following best explains this nongenetic source of variability?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Body weight alters the volume of distribution and clearance of the drug

choices.label: B
choices.text: Body weight changes the DNA sequence of the drug-metabolizing enzyme

choices.label: C
choices.text: Body weight changes the number of drug receptors expressed on target cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: Body weight determines whether phase 2 conjugation reactions occur at all

choices.label: E
choices.text: Body weight determines which HLA alleles present the drug to immune cells

explanation.summary: Body weight is a nongenetic factor that changes a drug's volume of distribution and clearance.
explanation.whyCorrect: Safe and effective prescribing requires identifying individual factors that cause clinically significant changes in pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics, including age, gender, and body weight. Body weight can affect the volume of distribution and clearance of a drug, so obese patients may require different dosing than those with lower body weight.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Body weight cannot alter the DNA sequence of a metabolizing enzyme gene.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Receptor number and type are set by receptor gene variants rather than by body weight.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Phase 2 conjugation occurs regardless of body weight; its rate is modified by genetic variants such as those in TPMT.
whyWrongByChoice.E: HLA alleles are inherited and determine immune presentation independently of a patient's body weight.
